summary: The Antoran Wastes lie inside the rift that splits Argus, and there is nothing left of them that is not fel. Antorus, the Burning Throne fills the western half — the Legion's own seat, built into the cliff — while the port at Terminus sends its fleets out under a portal spire in the south and the works around the Spirit Crucible grind in the north. The Army of the Light holds two footholds on the edge of it and the Illidari hold a third.
history: There were rich mines here once, in the Telaasti Reaches, and the building of Antorus swallowed them millennia ago; almost nobody remembers them. Everything since has been infrastructure for an invasion of everywhere else: a port to move ships, an armoury to defend it, and a crucible in the north to break souls into soldiers. Azeroth's campaign came at all three. The Army of the Light landed at Hope's Landing, Alleria worked the south against the Felfire Armory's guns while Illidan struck the crucible from the Veiled Den, and the throne itself was finally entered through a crack beneath an artillery platform — the main gates kill anything that walks up to them.

summary: The Arathi Highlands are rolling green hills and pine in southeastern Lordaeron, dry, cool and poor in everything except history: this is where Thoradin raised Strom and the first human empire. Stromgarde Keep in the southwest was contested for years by the Syndicate, the ogres and the trolls before the Alliance won it back under Danath Trollbane; Refuge Pointe is the Alliance camp in the north and Hammerfall, an old internment camp for orc prisoners, is the Horde's. Boulderfist ogres, Witherbark forest trolls and kobolds hold most of the ground between, and the entrances to Arathi Basin are here as well.
history: Thoradin united the human tribes some twenty-eight centuries before the Dark Portal and built Strom on this dry ground, chosen because the Amani could not ambush across it, with a great wall thrown up for good measure. Strom carried the empire through the Troll Wars and long after, until its noble families left for richer land in the north and Faldir took the last of Thoradin's line south to found Stormwind; what remained became Stromgarde. The Second War rolled over the highlands before the Alliance forced the orcs back across the Thandol Span. Stromgarde wanted the prisoners executed afterwards and was overruled, and Danath Trollbane ended up running the camps built instead — one of them here, at the village that became Hammerfall, until Thrall and Doomhammer emptied it. After Thoras Trollbane died the kingdom fell apart from within. His son Galen held a quarter of Stromgarde for years against the Syndicate, the Witherbark and the Boulderfist, was killed by Horde agents hunting Trol'kalar, and came back Forsaken; he turned on the Forsaken to take the keep for himself, and when the Ebon Blade destroyed him it came out that he had murdered his father in the first place. Both armies came back for the ruin in the Fourth War, and Stromgarde came out of that fight with Danath Trollbane crowned king.

summary: Ardenweald is where nature's spirits go to sleep and be made ready to wake up somewhere else. Wild Gods, ancients and loa arrive in the Winter Queen's forest as wildseeds, and the night fae pour anima into them until they are whole enough to be sent back through the Grove of Awakening. Enormous celestial trees anchor each grove and do the drawing; several of them are dead, because there has not been enough anima to go round for a long time.
history: The forest began with the Winter Queen and Marasmius alone, and grew as she raised the celestial trees; the tirnenn came with them and built the groves around each one. Every grove has its tree and its name, and the loss of one is permanent — Tirna Marwol went dark in the Darkreach long ago, Tirna Noch fell early in the drought and Tirna Rowen has held no wildseed since. When the anima stopped arriving the night fae had to start choosing which sleeping spirits to sustain and which to let end. The Drust, cursed to sit outside the cycle altogether, took the chance to force their way into the mists and try to steal a rebirth they were never owed.

summary: Ashenvale is the old-growth forest that is the night elves' mainland home, kept by the Sentinels and by the dryads and keepers who are Cenarius's children, with Astranaar on its island in a lake at the centre of the road. The Horde has held the eastern woods since the Third War and works them for timber out of Splintertree Post and the Warsong Lumber Camp, which is what the fighting here is about and why the Warsong Gulch battleground opens off Silverwing Grove in the south. Satyrs hold Xavian and Satyrnaar, furbolg tribes have gone feral in their villages, and naga come ashore on the Zoram Strand beside Blackfathom Deeps.
history: The kaldorei rebuilt into these woods over centuries after the Sundering and fought the War of the Satyr through them; when that ended the Cenarion Circle turned on the Druids of the Scythe, and Mel'Thandris Starsong died holding their worgen off her own people — she and the Scythe of Elune went into the ground at the shrine that carries her name. The Highborne who raised an arcane storm here were exiled rather than executed. When saronite began surfacing across the world, Fandral Staghelm's druids secretly cut six branches from Nordrassil and planted one of them in Ashenvale; it rooted into a great tree that fed the Emerald Dream into the forest and scoured the deposits out of it. Through the Long Vigil the druids slept in barrow dens under Tyrande's Sentinels. In the Third War the Warsong clan came for the timber, and Grommash Hellscream drank the Legion's blood and killed Cenarius with it; then Archimonde's host burned inland toward Hyjal, and Tichondrius's corruption of the northern woods made Felwood out of them. Illidan killed Tichondrius for the Skull of Gul'dan and stopped the taint spreading. Garrosh Hellscream came back for the timber after the Cataclysm with goblin shredders to cut it faster; Varian Wrynn and Genn Greymane's worgen fought the advance to a stop beside the Sentinels, and the Horde kept most of what it took.

summary: Ashran is an island in the Barrier Sea off the coast of Tanaan Jungle: ruined ogre country that both Azerothian factions landed on because the ground is full of artifacts. Stormshield and Warspear face each other across it as the expansion's faction cities, and the contested ground between them was Warlords of Draenor's open-world player-versus-player zone. Since Battle for Azeroth that fight has been folded into an instanced epic battleground, and the open island is still there, quiet, with its events switched off.
history: The island belonged to the Gorian Empire, ruled at one point by Kor'lok, and its towers, arenas and worked-out mines are what is left of that. Two ogre clans divide the ruins: the Ashmaul, who bind fire and field pyromancers and summoned elementals, and the smaller Gor'vosh in the south-eastern burial grounds, who raise the Ashmaul dead back up. The two loathe each other and everything else on the island. The Alliance and Horde came for the artifact fragments scattered across it, Harrison Jones digging for one side and Belloc Brightblade for the other, the Reliquary wanting the power and the Steamwheedle goblins stringing fragments into souvenirs; each faction has since cut its own entrance into the mines beneath.

summary: Azj-Kahet is the bottom of Khaz Algar and the last kingdom of living nerubians — the one the Scourge never took. Most of it is the City of Threads, a capital rebuilt on its own ruins so many times that height is rank: the favoured live at the top and the rest live in what is decaying underneath them. Queen Ansurek rules it in partnership with Xal'atath, which is not a popular arrangement; the wilds beyond the city hold niffen traders, deepwalkers and haranir, and a conspiracy called the Severed Threads is working the whole time to cut the queen down.
history: This kingdom survived what Azjol-Nerub did not. Its people came through mythic wars that repeated across millennia by outliving everyone who started them, and then kept to their own depths for a very long time. Xal'atath arrived after the Old Gods were dead and the Black Empire finished, and offered Ansurek the end of that isolation: a way back to power, and a means of remaking chosen nerubians into something stronger. The queen took it. Her people now harvest the Black Blood of the Old Gods inside Nerub-ar Palace and throw swarm after swarm at the Arathi in the cavern above. Enough nerubians disagreed to start conspiring instead.

summary: Azsuna is the south-western Broken Isles, a coast of pale ruins and olive groves left over from the night elf empire and haunted by the people who lived in them. Prince Farondis and his court are still here and cannot die, drifting through Nar'thalas; the blue dragons of the Azurewing keep a ley pool inland, and the naga work the shallows for what Azshara wants. Above it all the Wardens hold their prison on the Isle of the Watchers, and the Legion has burned a landing at Faronaar.
history: Prince Farondis was one of the few Highborne rulers who would not follow Queen Azshara into her bargain with Sargeras. His plan was to destroy the Well of Eternity outright, using the Tidestone of Golganneth kept in Nar'thalas Academy, and a young noble of his own court sold him to the queen before he could. Azshara's answer was to break the Tidestone and let what came out of it wash over the whole province: the city fell and its people were left unable to die, which is why the ghosts still keep their courtesies. The Sundering left the ruins as an island. Ten thousand years on, the Tidestone was fought over again, this time with Azshara's naga.

summary: Azuremyst Isle is the southern half of the Azuremyst Isles off northwestern Kalimdor, evergreen and purple-flowered, with fog, thunderstorms and the occasional arcane squall rolling over it. The draenei live here because their ship came down here: the Exodar's hull is now their capital, Azure Watch is the town between it and the sheltered Ammen Vale where every draenei starts, and the crystals thrown out by the crash are still working their way through the local wildlife. The Stillpine furbolgs are friends, the Bristlelimb are not, and Wrathscale naga hold the night elf ruins on the west coast.
history: The isles were the untamed western edge of ancient Kalimdor, left unsettled on purpose by the Kaldorei Empire as hunting ground, and the Sundering broke them off the continent with their plants and animals aboard. The night elves eventually abandoned them and the furbolgs and wildkin had the place to themselves for centuries. Then the Exodar, sabotaged by Kael'thas's followers, came down on the isle; the survivors salvaged what they could, built Azure Watch and started hunting down what the crystals had poisoned. Admiral Odesyus's flotilla was grounded on the south shore around the same time, which is how the draenei met the Alliance. The Legion came for the naaru O'ros later and was beaten off.

summary: The Badlands are dry canyon country in southeastern Khaz Modan: cracked flats inside a ring of mountains, the Lethlor Ravine cut down the eastern side and the Scar of the Worldbreaker burnt across the west where Deathwing came up. Almost everyone here is digging — the Explorers' League and the blood elf Reliquary compete over Uldaman and the Tomb of the Watchers, the Dark Iron clan works out of Angor Fortress, and the Steamwheedle goblins at Fuselight sell to whoever is nearest. New Kargath is the Horde's, Dragon's Mouth the Alliance's, and Dustbelcher ogres and black dragons hold the ground between them.
history: The oldest thing in the region is Uldaman, the titan vault in the northeastern hills where the earthen were made and where the dwarves' own beginnings are recorded, which is why so much traffic here is archaeological. The Second War came through when the Horde held all Khaz Modan for its ore and oil: Black Tooth Grin orcs escorted Cho'gall across these flats to inspect the refineries at Grim Batol, and killed a Stromgarde patrol on the way. Thrall later sent the Kargath Expeditionary Force to found the only Horde outpost in Khaz Modan and go after Rend Blackhand, while Ironforge prospectors and Steamwheedle goblins arrived for reasons of their own. The Cataclysm buried Kargath under an avalanche and left the long burnt scar across the west; New Kargath was raised nearby.

summary: Bastion is the kyrian realm of the Shadowlands: white spires and gardens under an endless bright sky, every part of it built around one process. The Arbiter sends souls inclined to service here to be stripped of the burdens they died carrying, and those that come through it earn wings and become the Ascended, who carry other souls in turn. That machinery is not running cleanly — the Forsworn, aspirants who broke rather than let go, hold parts of the realm against their own kind.
history: Bastion was wild before it was orderly; its beasts were dangerous until the Ascended Korinna tamed them. Long ago the Void came for the Shadowlands through here and caught the kyrian unready, and Agthia, the Paragon of Courage of that age, spent her own life to throw back Tezulat the Annihilator — the hulks of the colossi from that day still lie where they fell. A devourer incursion later killed Mercia, the first Paragon of Humility. The realm's worst wound was internal: doubt about whether the forgetting demanded of every aspirant was a mercy or a theft split the kyrian, the Forsworn turned on the temples, and their sympathies ran as far as the Maw itself.

summary: Blade's Edge Mountains is northwestern Outland: forested mesas and dusty canyons separated by ridges of stone spikes sharp enough to have given the place its name, with the highest plateaus reachable only by flight. It is ogre country, ruled from the top by the gronn and by Gruul the Dragonkiller, whose Bladespire and Bloodmaul subjects fight each other for his favour. Sharing it are the half-ogre Mok'Nathal, arakkoa in the northern woods, druids at Evergrove, gnomish tinkers at Toshley's Station, and the black dragons and nether drakes left over from Deathwing's visit.
history: Two places became one here: Gorgrond and Frostfire Ridge, fused when Draenor broke apart, keeping the spikes Frostfire was known for. This was ogre country, and Thunderlord country. Bladespire Hold was a Gorian stronghold left an isolated city-state once the orcs destroyed Goria, and its imperator bred ogres to orcs for an army — the Mok'Nathal, who rebelled under Leoroxx, pulled the fortress down and withdrew. After the Second War Deathwing bargained passage to Draenor and hid clutches of eggs here, and the gronn fought his flight for the ground. Khadgar stripped the plates off Deathwing's back while Gruul nearly finished him by hand; the dragons left behind were dragged out of the sky and impaled on the spires, and that is how he became the Dragonkiller. The eggs that survived hatched, warped by the nether, as the Netherwing.

summary: The Blasted Lands are the red, lightning-struck desert that the southern Black Morass was cooked into when the Dark Portal opened, and the portal still stands at the centre of them with Outland on the far side. Nethergarde Keep holds the northern rim for the Alliance and Okril'lon Hold for the Horde, both built to watch the gate rather than each other. The one green thing in the region is the Tainted Forest in the southwest, a druid's failed attempt to bring the land back, corrupted like everything else, with the fishing village of Surwich at its edge.
history: This was the southern Black Morass, marshland, until the Dark Portal was raised in it and the orcs came through to fall on Stormwind. What bled off the gate cooked the ground into what Nethergarde's garrison took to calling the Blasted Lands; the living half to the north was renamed the Swamp of Sorrows for the Second War's dead. Khadgar and the Kirin Tor built the keep to watch the rift. Two years on Ner'zhul widened it with the Skull of Gul'dan, and Danath Trollbane's army was destroyed contesting the site — he walked back its only survivor. The Sons of Lothar marched past him and destroyed the portal from the Draenor side. Demons stayed anyway: Kazzak held the Tainted Scar, Razelikh bought the Shadowsworn a third of an amulet each, and the Ironmarch later invaded through the rebuilt gate.

summary: Bloodmyst Isle is the northern half of the Azuremyst Isles and it is red: crystals from the Exodar's crash buried themselves in the ground here, and what leaked out of them stained the soil, tinged the pines crimson and turned most of the wildlife hostile. Blood Watch, built out of salvaged ship pods, is where the draenei work at undoing it, with Kessel's Crossing on the clean southern strip that the blight never reached. Satyrs hold Axxarien and Nazzivian, naga hold the reef, and the ship's leaking power core still sits in the middle of it all at the Vector Coil.
history: The night elf city of Loreth'Aran stood on this island, and its riders rode green dragons that Ysera herself had blessed, until Razormaw led the black flight down on them in the Dragon Wars and killed the city and its dragons together; the Sundering finished the job and left ruins on scattered islets. The draenei arrived and named the place Silvergale before they understood what their crash had done to it. The Sunhawks, under the eredar Sironas, tried to turn the wrecked power core into a gate for reinforcements out of Outland and were broken. Years later Velen found demons had been feeding the corruption all along, and only once they were burned out could the island start to heal.

summary: The Borean Tundra is the flat, treeless southwestern corner of Northrend, a wind-scoured plain of red and brown lichen where mammoth and rhino herds graze and tuskarr stone elders mark the fishing routes along the coast. It is where most travellers first set foot on the continent: the Horde's Warsong Hold and the Alliance's Valiance Keep sit within a few days' march of each other, neither zone belonging to either side. Tuskarr, taunka, magnataur and blue dragons share it with naga at the southern ruins and Scourge holding the old nerubian temple city in the east.
history: The ruins here are nerubian, and they are the oldest thing in the tundra — some hold that this coast was once a stretch of Azjol-Nerub pushed up into daylight, and that whoever tried living above ground gave it up. The tuskarr came next; Kaskala has stood for centuries, with the smaller villages budding off it as families divided. Drakkari hunting parties drifted down from Zul'Drak more recently and keep no fixed ground. When the war against the Lich King opened, both armies chose this shore to land on. The Horde raised Warsong Hold under Garrosh Hellscream and found the taunka, an offshoot of the tauren long thought lost; the Alliance built Valiance Keep and the farms of Farshire behind it.

summary: The Broken Shore is the black island in the south-east of the Broken Isles, dragged up off the sea floor by Gul'dan during the Second War because the Tomb of Sargeras was on it. That tomb is the Legion's door into Azeroth, and the demons built a city and a fortress around it. Deliverance Point on the western shore is where the class orders regrouped after the battle that killed a Warchief, a King and a Highlord, and Acherus hangs over the eastern end.
history: The island was called Thal'dranath and was part of Suramar, with the Temple of Elune standing on it, until the Sundering put it under the sea. The Guardian Aegwynn chose that sunken temple to hide the body of Sargeras' avatar, and its power warped the place into the Tomb that bears his name. Gul'dan raised the island in the Second War, opened the Tomb and was torn apart by what came out. Illidan took the Eye from it after the Third War. When a second Gul'dan reopened the portal, Azeroth's combined armies landed and were broken here; the survivors came back as the Armies of Legionfall.

summary: The Burning Steppes are ash, black rock and open lava between Redridge and the Searing Gorge, and the only overland road from Stormwind north to Khaz Modan runs across them. Blackrock Mountain stands on the northern ridge, and the Blackrock orcs, the black dragonflight and the Firegut ogres hold most of the ground under it. Against them there is Chiselgrip and Flamestar Post, run by the Thorium Brotherhood, the Horde's perch at Flame Crest and whatever the Alliance still keeps at Morgan's Vigil.
history: This was the northern Redridge range, green once like the rest of it. Then came the War of the Three Hammers: Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan, exiled from Ironforge, reached for something to win it and woke Ragnaros. Mountains melted, Blackrock Mountain rose out of the blast, and the country either side of it became the Searing Gorge and these steppes. Orcs arrived in the First War and reached for the same power; Ragnaros burned the warlocks who tried it, and Cho'gall's bargaining with the Old Gods won the Shadow Council only Blackrock Spire, as a hiding place. They held it until the Alliance besieged it late in the Second War — Orgrim Doomhammer killed Anduin Lothar at the volcano's foot and lost the war for the trouble. The Cataclysm put Deathwing's own cult in the depths of the mountain, and what the Twilight's Hammer wanted from the two dead dragons it dug up there — Nefarian, killed in his own lair, and Sinestra, Deathwing's consort — was not muscle but method: reanimated on void magic and obedient, she went back to breeding twilight dragons and he to forcing out another generation of chromatics. The Blackrock clan returned above them, pushed south into Redridge, and was pardoned into the Horde.

summary: Crystalsong Forest is the landlocked wood at the centre of Northrend, and every tree in it is glass — the whole forest was turned to crystal in a single botched spell and has stayed that way. What moves through it are the warped remnants of what was living when the spell went off: crystal dryads, satyrs and drifting elven spirits among the Ruins of Shandaral. Dalaran floats overhead since the Kirin Tor brought the city north, with the Silver Covenant at Windrunner's Overlook and the Sunreavers at Sunreaver's Command in two ruined Highborne towers, and the blue dragonflight holding the Azure Front below.
history: It was called Moonsong, and the Kaldorei Empire kept an outpost here named Shandaral to store arcane relics. The Sundering cut it off from everything, and its Highborne were left without a source of power and slowly failing. Watching blue dragons crystallise living things and draw energy from them, they infiltrated the Nexus to learn how, and stole relics while they were there. The dragons came for Shandaral. The sorcerers gathered on a cliff meaning to crystallise a piece of the forest and use it as a weapon, and lost control of it: the spell took the whole forest at once, shattering nearly everything alive and binding the dead to wander it. Dalaran arrived above it thousands of years later.

summary: Dalaran is the Kirin Tor's flying city, a magocracy under the Council of Six that lifted itself off the ground rather than be besieged again, and then went where the war was — Northrend, the Broken Isles, and finally Khaz Algar. It is neutral by charter: both factions keep quarters in it and are expected to behave, which has held better in some centuries than others. It is also gone. Xal'atath drained it into the Dark Heart and broke it apart over the Isle of Dorn, and the pieces lie along the Tranquil Strand; the versions still walked in are earlier ones, above Crystalsong Forest and the Broken Isles.
history: Magi of Arathor founded it as a city-state after the Troll Wars, on the southern shore of Lordamere Lake, and the Kirin Tor ruled it out of the Violet Citadel with the deepest library of human history anywhere. The Scourge besieged it and Archimonde pulled it down; the survivors came back, walled the heart of it in a dome and eventually raised the whole city into the air so that nothing walking could ever reach them. From there it followed the wars. It hung over Northrend for the campaigns against Malygos and the Lich King, admitted blood elves and high elves as rival delegations, expelled the Horde in a single afternoon after a theft, moved to the Broken Isles for the Legion, and ended over Khaz Algar.

summary: Darkshore is a long misted strip of northwestern coast, evergreen forest between the mountains and a rocky beach littered with ten-thousand-year-old ruins. It has been broken twice: the Cataclysm destroyed Auberdine outright and left a vortex of raw energy turning in the middle of the zone, and the Fourth War turned the whole coast into a battlefield the night elves had to take back by force. Lor'danel in the north and the Grove of the Ancients in the south are what the kaldorei still hold; naga, satyrs, grell and feral furbolgs have the rest, along with whatever the Horde left behind.
history: Two cities stood here before the Sundering, Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, and their lord Athrikus Narassin promised to save his people and instead sealed their souls in gems to power himself. Everything the night elves built afterward failed except Auberdine. Fandral Staghelm's druids planted Teldrassil from this coast. The Cataclysm then wrecked Darkshore more thoroughly than almost anywhere on Azeroth — Auberdine flattened, the ground split, whirlpools and storms — and Malfurion Stormrage went to the Eye of the Vortex and called on Cenarius's power to keep the strip from sliding into the sea. The survivors founded Lor'danel. Then the Horde marched through on its way to burn Teldrassil, and Maiev Shadowsong and the Gilneans took the coast back.

summary: Darnassus was the night elf capital, grown into the western boughs of Teldrassil around the Temple of the Moon and guarded by Sentinels and ancients — and it is ash. Sylvanas ordered the World Tree burned at the opening of the Fourth War with the city and most of its people still inside, and nothing that stands there now is lived in. The surviving kaldorei, the Sisterhood and the druids have made their home since in Bel'ameth, grown in the branches of Amirdrassil.
history: Mortality came as a shock after the Third War, and a faction of druids under Fandral Staghelm answered it by planting a new World Tree off the northern coast of Kalimdor, hoping to buy their people's immortality back. Darnassus rose among its branches: the Temple of the Moon for Tyrande and the sisterhood, a terrace for the Sentinels, an enclave for the druids, and a lake with bridges over it. Malfurion returned to find Fandral had been turned by Xavius and was the reason the tree was sickening; the Aspects blessed it once he was imprisoned. Gilnean refugees were given an oak of their own to live in. Then came the War of the Thorns, and the Horde put the whole tree to the torch.

summary: Deadwind Pass is a dead grey canyon between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows: no herbs, no ore, nothing living but vultures and spiders, and a wind off the rock that never lets up. Karazhan stands at the southern end, Medivh's tower on its nexus of ley lines, abandoned and full of dark enchantment since Khadgar and Lothar killed him inside it. Deadwind ogres camp in the Vice, ghosts fill the ruined village and the cellars under it, and the only welcome company is the handful of Violet Eye mages sent to find out what the tower is doing.
history: This land was killed on purpose. Sargeras sent Sataiel, the first necrolyte on Azeroth, with the scythe Ulthalesh to reap everything living here, and when they were gone she turned the blade on the ground: the trees withered, the marsh dried, the sky went the colour of a shroud, and the nexus she made blew open the crater. Aegwynn built Karazhan on it in secret six hundred years before the First War, and her son Medivh came there as a young man for the year she spent teaching him what a guardian was. The Kirin Tor sent Khadgar as an apprentice who was really a spy, and it was Khadgar who put the blade in when Lothar's war party came for the possessed guardian. The fel energy loosed by that death cursed the pass and blighted Brightwood into Duskwood.

summary: Deepholm is the earth domain of the Elemental Plane: one enormous cavern of ageless stone with no sun, no wind and no ceiling anyone has found, lit only by mineral clusters the size of buildings. Therazane the Stonemother rules it and has no patience for outsiders, which is most of the reason visitors have a hard time here. The Earthen Ring hold the Temple of Earth at its centre, with stone troggs, the Deepholm earthen and the Twilight's Hammer sharing the rest.
history: Therazane the Stonemother was one of four Elemental Lords who held Azeroth for the Old Gods. Archaedas undermined the citadel she shut herself in and Freya's roots pulled it down on her; Ra and Helya then built the Elemental Plane out of four linked domains and put her in this one with every earth elemental alive. Deathwing knew the place: carried here to recover after Grim Batol, he had elementium plates bolted over his splitting hide in the Stonecore beneath the Temple of Earth. Whole again, he tore up through the roof of the world, shattering the World Pillar that held Deepholm and Azeroth apart. That break is the Cataclysm: two realms grinding together, elementals loose on the surface. Therazane has treated every outsider as an enemy since. The Earthen Ring took the temple back and reassembled the pillar.

summary: Desolace is the centaur homeland on the western coast, a grey bone-strewn waste under permanent storm — except that it is not entirely a waste any more. The Cataclysm brought water back to the middle of the zone and the Cenarion Circle has grown the Cenarion Wildlands there, green and treed, with Karnum's Glade at its heart. Around that the old zone continues: four centaur tribes at each other's throats, the Burning Blade dug in at Thunder Axe Fortress, demons at Mannoroc Coven, Hatefury satyrs in the ruins of Sargeron, naga pushing onto the northern shore, and Maraudon still open in the Valley of Spears.
history: This was Mashan'she, fertile grassland the tauren grazed, until their shaman spent decades trying to wake what they took for the Earth Mother beneath it and woke Princess Theradras instead. She drank the land dry to rebuild herself, and the dying was felt as far as the Emerald Dream. Cenarius's son Zaetar came to imprison her, fell in love with her instead, and fathered the centaur — who murdered him, drove the tauren out, and spent centuries at war with them. Much later Theradras drove her children into a killing frenzy to save them from the Horde; the Horde allied with Warug's Magram, went into Maraudon and killed her, and the Magram have led the united tribes uneasily since. Alexstrasza withdrew into this waste in grief after Wyrmrest, and Thrall came here to show her what Korialstrasz had really done.

summary: Dornogal is the earthen city at the centre of the Isle of Dorn, greener than a city of living stone has any right to be, built around the mouth of the Coreway — the titan shaft that runs down into Azeroth itself. The Council of Dornogal rules it, and after thousands of years of isolation in Khaz Algar its people have their own turns of phrase and their own way of doing things. Both factions keep embassies here now, and the portals in its halls are the way to the Ringing Deeps, Azj-Kahet, Undermine and K'aresh.
history: It was raised as the fortress guarding the Coreway, the shaft the titan-forged sank so the worldsoul could be studied without being harmed, and named for the watchers Dornic and Galan. Isolation did the rest: no contact with anyone for thousands of years, an earthen society running on the Edicts and on memories filed away in the Archive at the end of each rotation. When Adelgonn and the Stonebound broke with the Edicts and walked out, the city lost people it could not replace and began to run down. Then Dalaran fell out of the sky nearby, the nerubians came up through the Coreway in the confusion, and Dornogal took in the survivors of a city it had never heard of.

summary: The Dragonblight is the frozen wasteland at the heart of southern Northrend, and it is where dragons go to die — the plain is littered with their bones, and a shrine for each of the five flights stands among them. Wyrmrest Temple rises at the centre, titan-built and neutral ground for the dragonflights. Around the edges sit everybody else: Alliance at Wintergarde Keep and Fordragon Hold, Horde at Agmar's Hammer and Venomspite, tuskarr at Moa'ki Harbor, Argent Crusade in the south, the Scarlet Onslaught on the eastern coast, and the entrance to nerubian Azjol-Nerub in the west.
history: Galakrond ate his way across the north until the keeper Tyr talked five proto-dragons into hunting him; the monster came down on this plain and his bones are still in it. The keepers returned to pour the Pantheon's power into those five, making them the Aspects, and raised Wyrmrest Temple over the site; dragons have died here ever since. Aegwynn fought the Avatar of Sargeras here. Arthas landed at the Forgotten Shore, burned his own ships and went north for Frostmourne. Kel'Thuzad brought Naxxramas down over Wintergarde and was boarded and gutted for it. Both armies then took Angrathar, the gate into Icecrown — and Forsaken apothecaries shelled the field with plague, killing Bolvar Fordragon, Dranosh Saurfang and everyone else on it. In the Cataclysm the Twilight's Hammer besieged Wyrmrest while the Aspects and Thrall charged the Dragon Soul inside.

summary: The Dread Wastes are the mantid homeland, the southern half of the country beyond the Serpent's Spine, and they are rotting: sha corruption has run through the soil and up into the kypari trees the whole civilisation draws its amber from. The Heart of Fear at the centre is the empress's palace and the source of it. Klaxxi'vess is the one place an outsider is made welcome, because the Klaxxi have decided their empress must die and are short of hands.
history: The mantid have always swarmed and always recovered from it. What broke the pattern was the Sha of Fear taking Grand Empress Shek'zeer. Under her the swarm stopped resisting corruption and embraced it — in themselves, in the amber, in the sacred trees the culture is built around — and hurled itself at the wall a decade early, on more fronts than it could feed. The Klaxxi, elders who keep what the mantid actually are and who wake their paragons out of amber when the need is real, read that as the end of their people and called for the empress's death. A dying elder cut Kil'ruk the Wind-Reaver free to begin it. She fell in the Heart of Fear; the sha saw the odds and fled the wastes.

summary: Drustvar is the western end of Kul Tiras: cold, forested, mountainous, and harder to live in than anywhere else in the kingdom. It supplies most of the realm's ore and a good deal of its infantry, and it answers to House Waycrest from Corlain. It is also the old country of the Drust, whose ruins stand in the hills, and whose death magic came back through the Heartsbane Coven to curse whole villages and set wicker constructs walking.
history: The Drust, vrykul who came here by sea after the Sundering, held the archipelago for millennia before humans of the Arathorian Empire landed around 2,700 BDP. The Drust refused every offer of peace and raided the new settlements out of this region for years. The Waycrest family answered by founding the Order of Embers, and the Thornspeakers broke with their own kin to help; Arom Waycrest finally took the Drust city of Gol Osigr and killed King Gorak Tul, and was made lord of the region for it. Gorak Tul was not gone. During the Fourth War he answered Lady Meredith Waycrest's plea to save her dying husband, and the price was the coven that swallowed Corlain.

summary: Dun Morogh is the snow country of northwestern Khaz Modan, the tallest range in the Eastern Kingdoms and the homeland of both dwarves and gnomes. Ironforge is cut into the mountain at its heart and Gnomeregan into the foothills of Chill Breeze Valley, though the gnomes irradiated their own capital and now work out of New Tinkertown at its door. Kharanos and Coldridge Valley are where new dwarves and gnomes begin; Frostmane ice trolls and troggs hold the hills and passes around them.
history: The Frostmane ice trolls had this country first, having broken from the Drakkari after the Sundering. Gnomes emerged from Uldaman three thousand years before the Dark Portal and built fortified holds in the rock; dwarves followed five centuries later, drawn to the peaks on the horizon, and cut Ironforge beneath the tallest. The two have been useful to each other since: dwarven stonework raised Gnomeregan and gnomish engineering repaid it, while the dwarven armies broke the trolls' hold and drove them into the hills. When Doomhammer came for Khaz Modan's ore and oil the dwarves brought their own tunnels down behind them and gave up the outlying holds; both capitals held anyway, so the Horde settled for penning them in and working the mines it had taken. Gnomeregan survived that only to be lost from within during the Third War.

summary: Durotar is the orcs' homeland on Kalimdor's eastern coast — red rock, cracked soil, scorpids and canyons — with Orgrimmar set into the mountains at its northern end and the Darkspear trolls holding the Echo Isles off the southern shore. The Southfury broke its banks in the Cataclysm and turned the western strip to marsh, and Garrosh Hellscream answered by ringing the zone in iron: battlements, watchtowers and the Dranosh'ar Blockade drawn across the ground in front of the city gates. Kul Tiran marines still sit in the ruins of Tiragarde Keep and in a foothold west of Sen'jin Village.
history: The land was quilboar country, the eastern edge of the Barrens, until Thrall's Horde drove the Razormane out during the Third War. After Mount Hyjal the orcs settled here and named it for Durotan, Thrall's murdered father, raising Orgrimmar with tauren and Darkspear help. The peace lasted until Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet arrived to finish the orcs off; Rexxar unravelled the plot, and Jaina let her father die rather than break the truce. The Darkspear spent years exiled from the Echo Isles by the traitor Zalazane and killed him only after the Lich King fell. Then the Cataclysm pushed the Southfury over a quarter of the zone and burned much of Orgrimmar, and Garrosh rebuilt both as a garrison.

summary: Duskwood is the fiefdom south of Elwynn where the sun does not come up: twisted trees under a standing black fog, left that way by the fel energy of Medivh's death. Darkshire holds the centre and the Night Watch patrols the road through it, against the dead of Raven Hill Cemetery, the Nightbane worgen in the orchards and the Splinter Fist ogres at Vul'Gol. In the north stands the Twilight Grove, one of Fandral Staghelm's great trees, with a way into the Emerald Dream open at its roots.
history: A branch cut from Nordrassil was planted here four and a half thousand years before the Dark Portal and grew into the tree at the Twilight Grove. The region was southern Elwynn then, called Brightwood, with Grand Hamlet and Raven Hill for towns. Blackhand's raiders razed villages here in the First War, and Brightwood was one of three fiefs the Horde took before closing on Stormwind. Then Medivh died at Karazhan and the fel energy loosed spilled over the border; the trees blackened, the spiders swelled to monstrous size, and the wolves fled north into Elwynn. Morbent Fel's necromancy filled the graveyards afterwards. Velinde Starsong died here carrying the Scythe of Elune, and the artefact's long passage through these woods — lost, found, hunted by the Dark Riders — killed the Yorgen family and left the Nightbane pack behind.

summary: Dustwallow Marsh is a hot fog-bound swamp on Kalimdor's southeastern coast, thinly settled and mostly left to crocolisks, raptors and murlocs. The rocky island off its eastern shore held Theramore until Garrosh Hellscream's mana bomb erased the city, and the roads that once ran out to it are going back to the marsh. What is left is scattered: Brackenwall Village where the Stonemaul ogres take in the Horde, the goblin town of Mudsprocket in the southwest, Grimtotem at Blackhoof Village in the north, and the black dragonflight holding the Wyrmbog and the Dragonmurk in the south around Onyxia's Lair.
history: Nothing lived in this swamp but animals until Jaina Proudmoore brought her survivors here after Mount Hyjal and founded Theramore, throwing scout towers up along the road to the Barrens. Her father's fleet followed to destroy the young Horde and Daelin died in the fighting, which ended any pretence of peace between the factions. Rexxar killed the Stonemaul's tyrant and brought the ogres into the Horde; the black dragons later drove them out of their own village and up to Brackenwall. The Steamwheedle founded Mudsprocket and the Grimtotem took the north. The Shattering barely touched the place. Then Garrosh dropped a mana bomb on Theramore and the marsh has been quiet in a different way since.

summary: The Eastern Plaguelands are the badly damaged half of old Lordaeron's east: brown ground under an orange haze, enormous fungus, and animals that ought to have died years ago. Stratholme stands ruined at the northern edge, the Argent Crusade holds Light's Hope Chapel and a ring of retaken watchtowers meant as points of light across the middle, and Acherus, the death knights' floating hold, hangs over the far east. The Scourge's grip has been loosening for years, but Plaguewood, Tyr's Hand and the emptied towns between them are still nowhere to travel alone.
history: This was the Eastweald: farms and villages under Stratholme, the second city of the kingdom, and the ground the Church of the Holy Light chose for its greatest houses — Light's Hope and Tyr's Hand among them. Arthas came hunting Mal'Ganis, found Stratholme's people already carrying the plague, and killed them himself when Uther refused the order, which broke the Silver Hand and him with it. Lordaeron fell and the blight spread over everything. Alexandros Mograine's crusade held Tyr's Hand before splitting three ways, and Naxxramas hung over the Plaguewood until Kel'Thuzad was beaten inside it. Light's Hope Chapel bore the weight twice: his son Darion ran himself through on the corrupted Ashbringer there to free him, and the Lich King's own attack on the chapel later cost him the blade, his death knights and Tirion Fordring both.

summary: Elwynn Forest is the wooded heartland of Stormwind, a country of hardwoods, rivers and small farms running down from the foothills of the Burning Steppes to the Nazferiti, with the capital itself standing in its northwestern hills. Goldshire is its market town and Eastvale its lumber camp, and between them the smallholdings grow wheat, melons, pumpkins and grapes under heavy guard patrols. Kobolds hold the mines, Riverpaw gnolls camp along the forest's edge and murlocs have taken the lakes, but none of it threatens the kingdom.
history: Faldir's Arathi settlers came south from Lordaeron about twelve centuries before the Dark Portal and founded Stormwind in the valley this forest surrounds; villages followed. Gnolls burned Goldshire during the Gnoll War. In the First War thousands of orcs marched through these trees to ring the capital, and it was back through them that Lothar's knights, landed by sea behind the siege lines, charged to break the first assault; Goldshire was one of the last two towns to fall before the keep was finally sacked. Turalyon oversaw the return afterwards and Alonsus Faol saw Northshire Abbey rebuilt, but the masons who rebuilt the city were never paid, and the riots that followed killed Queen Tiffin and made the Defias. Much later the Shattering cracked the mountain wall open and Blackrock orcs burned the Northshire vineyards.

summary: The Emerald Dream is Azeroth as it would look if nothing had ever built on it — a spirit world outside the physical one, in layers, some of them discarded drafts of the planet. The part of it anyone walks is reached through the Dream Portal on the Ancient Bough in the Dragon Isles, where nature magic spills out into the Emerald Gardens. Merithra holds it as Aspect after her mother, the green flight keeps the Eye of Ysera, and Amirdrassil was grown here and carried out into the waking world when Fyrakk failed to burn it.
history: Freya either wove it during the Ordering or found it already there and set about tidying it, depending on whether you ask a titan-forged or a nature spirit. She planted G'Hanir, first and tallest of trees, and set Nymue at the Wellspring Temple to keep the pattern. Ysera was bound into an endless trance to watch the world from inside it, and her flight has guarded every doorway since, seeing both sides at once with their eyes shut. Cenarius was raised in it. After the War of the Ancients Ysera tied Nordrassil to the Dream, which is what lets druids sleep here and learn. And in one corner the Rift of Aln festered, and the Nightmare came out of it.

summary: Eredath was the jewel of Argus, the eredar's holiest and finest city, and it is the one part of the world that still looks like itself: a piece of city core torn loose and left floating above the ruin, its gardens and squares nearly intact. The Seat of the Triumvirate stands empty at the centre, and the Void has moved into it. Ethereals of the Shadowguard are working there for the darkened naaru held below, while the Army of the Light beams its people up from the surface to stop them.
history: This was where the eredar's three rulers sat and where their scholars taught; Archimonde came out of the Conservatory of the Arcane and led its orders. When Sargeras made his offer to the Triumvirate, two of the three took it, Velen ran, and the world that had been the pinnacle of eredar civilisation became the Legion's forge. Eredath survived better than anything else on Argus, because the deformation of the planet lifted its centre clear rather than burying it. What was left standing has since been claimed twice over: by the Legion, and by the Void that gathered around a fallen naaru beneath the Seat.

summary: Eversong Woods is now the whole mainland of Quel'Thalas: the golden forest held in perpetual spring, the old Ghostlands folded back into it, Silvermoon rebuilt at the northern tip and the Isle of Quel'Danas beyond that. The Dead Scar has closed over into the Tranquil Repose, though the Ruins of Deatholme at its southern end are held by the Twilight's Blade, the Amani still come down out of Zul'Aman in the east, and Daggerspine naga have taken the island off the western shore. Tranquillien, Fairbreeze and Suncrown are elven towns again, and the road through the Thalassian Pass joins the kingdom to the rest of the continent by land.
history: The Highborne took these woods from the Amani, made the Sunwell, and used its power to raise their cities and shape the forest, setting runestones through it to damp any magic that was not their own and locking the whole region into a permanent spring. Quel'Thalas stood for over seven thousand years. Red dragons enslaved by the Old Horde burned a third of the forest in the Second War without breaking Silvermoon's defences. Arthas managed what they could not: the Dead Scar torn through the middle of the woods, Sylvanas Windrunner killed, the capital broken and the south left a waste. Kael'thas destroyed the poisoned Sunwell and renamed his people for the dead, and Lor'themar and Rommath began the rebuilding that has now reached the far south.

summary: Felwood is a poisoned forest between Ashenvale and Winterspring, its ancients rotting where they stand, its wildlife mutated, and satyrs and infernals moving freely through it. The Emerald Circle works out of Emerald Sanctuary to undo that and has managed it in one place — Whisperwind Grove in the north, cleansed, with a clean moonwell in it. Against them the Shadow Council still holds Jaedenar under Lord Banehollow. Timbermaw Hold in the northeast belongs to one of the last two uncorrupted furbolg tribes left anywhere, and its tunnel is the way through to Moonglade and Winterspring.
history: This was the northern part of Ashenvale, and ordinary forest, until Archimonde decided to weaken the night elves by rotting the ground under them on his march to Hyjal. Tichondrius did the work with the Skull of Gul'dan, and everything that grew or walked here changed. Illidan Stormrage came for the skull, killed Tichondrius with it and took its power, and his brother banished him for that. The healing has been slow and grudging ever since. After the Cataclysm the druids cleansed the north into a grove, a satyr got far enough inside the order to lead it under a false name, ooze experiments cost the Horde its only outpost, and Bilgewater goblins began strip-mining Irontree.

summary: Feralas is a rainforest of enormous ancient trees filling the southwest of Kalimdor, green between the wastes of Desolace and the dry plateaus east of it, and full of Highborne ruins the elves no longer hold. The Gordunni ogres do: they have Dire Maul and are cutting the forest down around it, which has pushed the Woodpaw gnolls and the Feral Scar yetis east into each other. The Horde works out of Camp Mojache and the night elves out of New Feathermoon on the Forgotten Coast, both rebuilt after the Cataclysm, while naga hold the western isles and the Grimtotem besiege New Thalanaar in the east.
history: The Highborne city of Eldre'Thalas stood here and outlived the Sundering behind its walls, until Prince Tortheldrin bled his own people to keep a demon caged and the ogres moved into what was left; a Horde raid ended both him and Immol'thar. Cho'gall came through these woods after the Third War hunting Garona and later sent his cult back to teach the Gordunni magic, which is why the ogre expansion turned from raiding into corruption; the Stonemaul ogres and the Sentinels each broke that in their own way. The Cataclysm flooded Thalanaar and drowned the original Feathermoon on Sardor Isle, and Ysondre finally had the corrupted green dragon Taerar hunted down in the Lower Wilds.

summary: Frostfire Ridge is the north-western corner of Draenor, where glaciers and lava fields sit side by side and neither gives ground. The Frostwolf clan winters here among the great wolves, the Thunderlords hold the north from villages built inside the skeletons of dead colossals, and ogres hold the high rock above both. It is where the Horde's war on Draenor starts, and Bladespire Citadel is the prize that starts it.
history: Frostwolves and Whiteclaws settled the cold valleys when the clans scattered out of Gorgrond, living with the great wolves rather than against them; the Thunderlords made their name hunting gronn and their homes in the bones of what they killed. Above both sat the Gorian Empire, whose northern outpost was the fortress cut into Blade's Edge Mountain, and after Goria fell the Bladespire imperator bred ogres to orcs for numbers he lacked. Garad worked out that those Mok'Nathal were slaves, not soldiers; the rebellion he arranged with Leoroxx brought the fortress down and cost him a son. Generations on, the Iron Horde put its siege works in the middle of Frostwolf country, and Durotan's people took the citadel off the ogres with outside help. In the other Draenor, this land and Gorgrond were crushed together into the Blade's Edge Mountains.

summary: The Ghostlands are the southern half of the old Eversong forest, killed by the Scourge on their march to Silvermoon and left outside the magic that keeps the rest of Quel'Thalas in permanent spring. The Dead Scar runs up from Deatholme, the ruined villages are still walked by the elves who died defending them, and the blood elves hold only Tranquillien, the Farstrider Enclave and the Sanctum of the Sun, propped up by Forsaken help. Amani and Shadowpine trolls press from the east, where Zul'Aman sits behind its gate.
history: The Elrendar once merely divided this forest from the northern woods. Tranquillien was the largest town, the Windrunner family lived here, and three hidden ley-line nexuses held mooncrystals feeding the great shield over Silvermoon, while the Amani based their own power at Zul'Aman. The Old Horde burned the southern stretches in the Second War, the red dragons' fire outpacing Khadgar's storm. Then Arthas came: the elfgates fell, the mooncrystals were taken and their guardians killed, villages were razed and their dead raised as Scourge. Sylvanas's Farstriders were driven north, and the survivors named what was left the Ghostlands because the dead now outnumbered the living. Dar'Khan Drathir ruled the remnant from Deatholme until the elves killed him a second time.

summary: Gilneas is a storm-lashed peninsula in southwestern Lordaeron, sealed off from the rest of the world for a generation behind the Greymane Wall and largely emptied by the Cataclysm and the Forsaken invasion that followed it. Its people are Gilnean humans and the worgen they became, most of whom spent over a decade in exile before the kingdom was reclaimed under Queen Tess Greymane. The sun rarely reaches it: cobbled streets, gothic houses, marsh, lighthouses and a drowned town on the southwestern coast.
history: Gilneas began as an Arathorian city-state whose sailors found and settled Kul Tiras. Genn Greymane withdrew from the Alliance after the Second War and walled the peninsula off, leaving Lord Crowley's northern villages outside the stone. The Wall held against the Scourge only because Greymane let Arugal loose the worgen on them; the curse spread inward for years while the Northgate rebellion split the kingdom from within. The Cataclysm cracked the Wall, dropped Duskhaven into the sea, and Sylvanas talked Garrosh into handing her the invasion. Night elves landed to answer for a curse of their own making, and their Ritual of Balance cooled the worgen enough to put beast and human in one line. It was not enough. Liam Greymane took the arrow meant for his father, Sylvanas plagued the capital, and the survivors sailed for Darnassus. The peninsula stood empty for over a decade, and the Scarlet Crusade eventually moved into Gilneas City and made the cathedral its headquarters. Tess Greymane brought Calia Menethil's Forsaken in alongside the Alliance offensive that took the capital back, which her father would not lead beside the people who had killed his son; when the Crusade was broken and the Horde had gone, Genn abdicated and left her the crown.

summary: Gorgrond is northern Draenor, and it is a dead giant with a war being fought across him. The Breakers hold the dry north-west of mesas, geysers and sulphur pools; the Primals hold the green south-east, where the plants hunt; and the line between the two moves. Behind that natural wall the Blackrock clan works the Foundry on the north coast, feeding the Iron Horde its guns, its trains and its docks.
history: Aggramar shaped the giant Grond out of a mountain to fight the Evergrowth, and where he fell his body became this country — the ore is his blood, the ridges his spine. The fragments that broke off him fought on as the colossals and brought down Botaan, greatest of the sporemounds; the spores that burst out of it fell on plants to make the botani and on stone to begin the line that runs gronn, ogron, ogre and finally orc. Both halves of that inheritance are still here and still arguing over what the ground should be. The orcs came out of caves beneath it: the Blackrock learned to work blackrock ore here, the Dragonmaw broke rylaks to the saddle, and when the caverns overflowed, the clans that walked out became every clan there is. Gul'dan was born to one of them at the region's edge, exiled for his deformity, and killed them all when he came back holding fel. The Blackrock later built the Iron Horde's foundry here, and generations on the Mag'har held it against Yrel's Lightbound.

summary: The Grizzly Hills are pine forest and low green ridges in southeastern Northrend, the one part of the continent that looks like somewhere you could live. They are furbolg country: most of them keep to Grizzlemaw, a city built inside the stump of a failed World Tree. Around it are human trappers with their trading posts, the Venture Company clear-cutting and mining at Venture Bay, iron dwarves at Dun Argol, ice trolls holding Drak'Tharon Keep in the north, and a growing worgen cult working out of Bloodmoon Isle.
history: These woods were the cubhood range of the bear gods Ursoc and Ursol, and Ursoc ruled here long after. Around 4,500 BDP, with saronite spreading under Northrend, Fandral Staghelm's druids planted a branch of Nordrassil over the largest deposit and grew Andrassil, the Crown of the Snow. Its roots grew down to where Yogg-Saron lay chained; the Old God turned the tree, and everything near it went mad. The Cenarion Circle felled it and renamed the stump Vordrassil, the Broken Crown, and the furbolgs later built Grizzlemaw inside it. Trappers and goblin loggers came much later. During the war against the Lich King, Arugal was raised from the dead and set to making worgen of the trappers, while the Alliance and Horde fought over the timber and the bay.

summary: Hallowfall is a cavern the size of a country under western Khaz Algar, lit by Beledar — a vast crystal set in the ceiling that gives the place warmth, seasons and crops, and that the plants below turn to follow. The Hallowfall Arathi hold it from their capital at Mereldar, moving between farms, docks and dawntowers by airship, and they fight on two fronts: kobyss coming ashore out of the Undersea to the west, and nerubian swarms pushing up from Azj-Kahet. Beledar no longer only gives light; at intervals it turns, and everything under it goes to Void.
history: An emperor of the Arathi was given a vision by the Sacred Flame — a light somewhere beneath the world — and sent a fleet of airships across the Storming Sea to find it. The light found them first: it swallowed the expedition whole and put it down inside the cavern, wrecked and with no way home. That was a little over a decade ago. The ground fed them, so they stayed, named the crystal for the vision that brought them and built towns under it, taking the whole place for a revelation they were meant to keep clean. Then Sargeras drove his sword into Azeroth. The cavern shook, and from that day Beledar has been shifting into something else.

summary: Harandar is a bioluminescent jungle in a cavern under the world, and it is where the roots of every World Tree on Azeroth come together. The haranir live in it — a reclusive people who have kept sacred ground down here without the surface ever knowing, governed by their elders from the Den. Four of their villages sit under four sets of roots, and the Rift of Aln, which the Emerald Nightmare pours out of, is also here.
history: This place has no history of its own so much as it holds everyone else's: whatever happens to a World Tree above eventually shows in the roots below. Har'kuai in the northeast sits under Nordrassil, and water from the Well of Eternity runs down those roots, through the Vale of Mists and on into the Rift of Aln. Har'mara in the northwest sits under Teldrassil, whose roots have been smouldering since the Horde burned it in the Fourth War. Har'athir in the southeast has Amirdrassil's roots, new growth from a tree raised in the Dream. Har'alnor in the southwest reaches Shaladrassil. The haranir have guarded all of it quietly, as subterranean keepers of hidden land, for as long as anyone can establish.

summary: Hellfire Peninsula is the red, bone-strewn plain on the Outland side of the Dark Portal, and the first ground almost everybody sets foot on when they cross. Fel orcs hold Hellfire Citadel at its centre, the Burning Legion pours reinforcements onto the Stair of Destiny, and the Alliance at Honor Hold and the Horde at Thrallmar face each other across the middle of it. Blood elves, draenei and Cenarion druids all keep smaller outposts here, and three ruined forts between the citadel and the two towns change hands whenever either faction bothers to take them.
history: Tanaan Jungle grew out of a sporemound's corpse, and the Bleeding Hollow and Bonechewer lived under its canopy. Blackhand's masons raised the Citadel in the west as a council hall for the chieftains and a warlock workshop. On a peak beside it the clans drank Mannoroth's blood, and Gul'dan tore the mountain open in celebration: the Throne of Kil'jaeden. Warlock magic dried the jungle to red hardpan and reddened the sky, naming both peninsula and fortress. The Alliance Expedition came back through the Dark Portal, took the citadel in a day and sealed the rift as Draenor broke. When the portal reopened Kil'jaeden spent Kruul and Kazzak holding it, wanting both factions ashore and aimed at Illidan. The Alliance found Honor Hold still standing under Danath Trollbane, the Horde raised Thrallmar; the citadel fell last, Magtheridon bled dry inside.
factions: Sunfury blood elves of Falcon Watch

summary: Highmountain is the northern skyline of the Broken Isles: canyons, snow peaks and green valleys around one of the tallest mountains on Azeroth, with a whole second country of caverns under it. Its tauren are the descendants of Huln Highmountain and the range carries his name; they share the mountain, uneasily, with the drogbar who live below it. Right now the drogbar king Dargrul has the Hammer of Khaz'goroth, one tauren tribe has sold itself to the Legion, and the hunters of the Unseen Path keep their lodge on a peak above all of it.
history: Neltharion kept a lair and a vault in these mountains before he was Deathwing, and it was here that he made the Dragon Soul. When the Legion came the first time, Huln Highmountain pulled the scattered tauren tribes together and fought beside the night elves, and the range was named for him afterwards. He also fought the Old Gods' servants here, and when he could not beat them he warded their master's essence into the rock instead. His descendants and the drogbar then shared the mountain peaceably for generations. That ended with the third invasion: the drogbar took the tauren's hammer, the Bloodtotem went over to the demons as the Feltotem, and the old wards began to leak.

summary: Hillsbrad is the best-preserved corner of old Lordaeron, pine and pasture and working farmland that the plague largely missed, and it belongs to the Forsaken now. Tarren Mill is the largest town, the Sludge Fields beside it are an experiment carried out in the open, and Southshore was rendered uninhabitable with the New Plague before the Alliance came back to start clearing it. The Alterac Mountains along the north hold Crushridge ogres in the ruined capital, the crater where Dalaran used to stand, and the Stormpike dwarves who keep trying to come down out of them.
history: For pleasant farming country this has been fought over more often than anywhere else on Azeroth. Stormwind's refugees landed near Southshore after the First War and settled there. The Alliance of Lordaeron then mustered its whole strength in these foothills and the Horde came ashore unopposed anyway, dragonfire having scattered the fleet sent to stop it; the battle that followed was the first great land engagement of the Second War, where Gul'dan's death knights were used for the first time and the new paladins burned their fog off the field. Doomhammer broke into Durnholde himself to free Zul'jin from the cells. Thrall's orcs later took Southshore's ships to reach Kalimdor. The Forsaken finished what the wars started: Tarren Mill, the Sludge Fields, and Southshore poisoned outright.

summary: The Howling Fjord is the southeastern corner of Northrend, a country of green meadows, pine forest and cold rivers cut through by cliffs high enough that the settlements are joined by lifts rather than roads. It is vrykul land: Utgarde Keep, the hall of King Ymiron, stands over Daggercap Bay, and the villages around it have been reoccupied by giants who slept through several thousand years. Alliance settlers at Valgarde and Westguard, Forsaken apothecaries at Vengeance Landing and New Agamand, taunka at Camp Winterhoof, tuskarr on the Isle of Spears and pirates at Scalawag Point all keep footholds along the coast.
history: The vrykul were made here, and when the Curse of Flesh began turning them from stone to mortal flesh they went into the earth to sleep through it — which meant they also slept through the Sundering, and the fjord stood empty of them for millennia. Some accounts put Arthas Menethil's Northrend landing on this coast, where he burned his own ships to keep the 1st Legion from being recalled. Later the Lich King's Scourge went through the barrows waking the vrykul, who came out and took back the keeps they had abandoned. About the same time, pirates of the Northsea Freebooters looted a burial ground at Shield Hill and roused the kvaldir out of the sea. The Valiance Expedition made its beachhead into all of this.

summary: Hrothgar's Landing is a small fog-bound island in the North Sea off the top of Icecrown, reachable only by air, and the northernmost ground a traveller can freely stand on. The kvaldir took it from the tuskarr who lived there and hold it under Drottinn Hrothgar, using the mists as cover for raids on shipping in the strait below. It exists in play as the far end of the Argent Tournament: the daily work given to those the Argent Crusade has named Crusader.
history: There was a tuskarr village on this island — the dead scattered across it are still called Tualiq, which is probably what the place was called too — until Drottinn Hrothgar's kvaldir came out of the sea, killed or drove off everybody in it, and put his name on it instead. The kvaldir are the drowned spirits of vrykul raiders bound to Helya, and the ones who reached these waters were roused when pirates looted a vrykul burial ground down in the Howling Fjord. During the war against the Lich King the island became their staging point against the Silver Covenant and Sunreaver ships in the Sea Reaver's Run, with mistcallers hiding the fleet and deepcallers pulling krakens up out of the strait to break it.

summary: Icecrown is the Lich King's own ground: a glacier gone black with corruption in north-central Northrend, laced with saronite walls, gates and causeways joining one Scourge works to the next, with Icecrown Citadel standing over the Frozen Throne at the centre. Nothing here is native except the vrykul of Jotunheim and Ymirheim, and most of them serve. Against all of it stand the Argent Crusade at the Argent Vanguard and the tournament grounds in the northeast, the Knights of the Ebon Blade at the Shadow Vault, and the Alliance and Horde gunships in the sky above.
history: Kil'jaeden threw Ner'zhul's prison back into the world; it struck this glacier hard enough to be felt in the Grizzly Hills and made the Frozen Throne. The plague of undeath went out from there and took Northrend. Kil'jaeden later sent Illidan Stormrage to finish the Lich King; Arthas Menethil crossed beneath Azjol-Nerub to beat him to the ice, fought him in front of both armies and climbed to the throne; the Scourge built the citadel around it. Tirion Fordring judged a mass assault to be what the Lich King wanted and sent a strike force through the three saronite gates instead. Frostmourne broke on the Ashbringer, the souls in it turned on Arthas, and Bolvar Fordragon took the helm rather than leave the Scourge masterless. Sylvanas broke that helm here much later, tearing the sky open onto the Shadowlands.

summary: Ironforge is the dwarven capital, hollowed out of the mountain above Dun Morogh in rings around the Great Forge that named it — equal parts foundry, fortress and market, with stone overhead as well as underfoot. The Council of Three Hammers rules from the High Seat, Bronzebeard, Wildhammer and Dark Iron sharing a throne none of them won outright. The Deeprun Tram surfaces in Tinker Town, the Explorers' League runs its digs from the Hall of Explorers, and gnomes displaced from Gnomeregan make up much of the population.
history: The first dwarves left Uldaman around 2,500 BDP, delved into the tallest peak in Dun Morogh and raised a forge beside an altar to Khaz'goroth; the city grew around it and took its name. Gnomes were already neighbours and traded technology for masonry. When High King Modimus Anvilmar died the three clans went to war — the Bronzebeards kept the city, the Wildhammers and Dark Irons were driven out, and Thaurissan's revenge ended with Ragnaros pulled into the world. Every other dwarven hold fell to the Horde in the Second War and this one did not: Doomhammer weighed what storming it would cost, gave up, and left a clan to seal the gates instead. The nation sat the war out inside it. Word came in the Third War that Arthas had killed Muradin, and Magni took his grief to the Great Anvil and beat it into the Ashbringer, a blade made to answer Frostmourne; he gave it to Alexandros Mograine rather than carry it himself. Much later Magni turned to diamond, Moira seized the city, and the Council was the settlement that followed.

summary: The Isle of Dorn is the green surface of Khaz Algar, west of Pandaria and southeast of Kalimdor: waterfalls, ironwood forest and open mountain country with the earthen city of Dornogal at its middle. The Council of Dornogal governs it, and the villages around them are earthen too, with kobolds squatting in a hillside graveyard, fungarians in the southern basin and nerubians dug into a mine on the north shore. Dalaran's wreckage lies along the Tranquil Strand, which is what brought both factions here.
history: When the Elemental Lords ruled the world and this was still part of Kalimdor, the land answered to Al'Akir. The titans' surveyors filed it as Sector AR-938 and sent a contingent of earthen to look into an anomaly in a fissure. What the keepers got back was unsettling: those earthen began behaving like the ones taken by the curse of flesh, though they had never met them and shared nothing with them. Archaedas set the watchers Dornic and Galan over them, and the earthen eventually rose against Dornic for how he treated them. They named the place Khaz Algar and were left alone with it for thousands of years — until a magical city fell out of the sky onto their beach.

summary: The Isle of Quel'Danas is the northernmost of the three parts of Quel'Thalas, an island whose whole purpose is the Sunwell — the fount Dath'Remar made from a stolen vial of the Well of Eternity, destroyed by the elves themselves and since restored as a source of Light as well as arcane. Sun's Reach is the harbour and staging town, the Magisters' Terrace overlooks the well, and Dawnstar Village sits on the shore below. It is a front line again: Xal'atath's Devouring Host has struck the island, and the Vanguard of the Light musters here against her.
history: Dath'Remar's exiled Highborne emptied their stolen vial into a lake here some sixty-eight centuries before the Dark Portal, and the fount that erupted made the high elves what they became. Arthas came for it in the Third War, freezing a bridge across the strait, killing High King Anasterian Sunstrider on the way, and using the well to raise Kel'Thuzad as a lich — which fouled it, and through it everything the elves had built. Kael'thas concluded the corrupted well would eventually kill his people and had it destroyed outright. The Shattered Sun Offensive landed here later to stop him reopening it as a door for Kil'jaeden, and the well was restored in the aftermath.

summary: The Isle of Thunder is what stayed above water when the Thundering Mountain sank: the peak of Lei Shen's original seat, northwest of Townlong Steppes and walled off by mists until he came back to it. The Throne of Thunder stands on it, and the resurrected Thunder King has rebuilt an army there out of mogu, Zandalari and whatever his forges can turn out. The Kirin Tor Offensive and the Sunreaver Onslaught have landed on opposite shores and are racing each other inland as much as they are fighting him.
history: Before Lei Shen there was something the mogu answered to on this mountain. He killed it and took the title, then ruled Pandaria from here until he died, after which his successors moved the capital to Mogu'shan Palace and let the place empty. The Sundering dropped the mountain into the sea and left only the summit above the waves, and over the following ten thousand years Pandaria filed the island under legend. The Zandalari corrected that: they carried Lei Shen's body away to be resurrected, and he returned to a fortress that had been waiting for him. Dalaran's own split answered it — Jaina's mages on one shore, Lor'themar's Sunreavers on the other, and the Shado-Pan Assault interested only in the throne.

summary: K'aresh is the ethereals' homeworld, and it is in pieces: an arid desert planet whose twin suns were eaten and whose sky went from saffron to Void-purple, now a husk with habitable fragments strung around it. Ve'nari's K'aresh Trust has moved Tazavesh back home and is trying to grow the place green again under purchased eco-domes, while the Wastelanders survive on the debris and the Shadowguard feed the Manaforge at Shadow Point. What that manaforge is for is bringing Dimensius back.
history: Before the Void, this was a desert world of city-states — Tazavesh, Ma'nussa, Sufaad and the rest — ruled by a Council of Oracles who could hear the planet's worldsoul sing and renewed their oaths to him in ritual. Then Dimensius arrived and opened gateways to the Void all around the sky. The K'areshi threw up shields fed by ribbons that turned any energy into arcane; the shields held, and the arcane burned their bodies off them, which is where ethereals come from. They fought him to a standstill until he could summon armies, and fled into the Nether and the Shadowlands. Everyone believes he destroyed the world. He did not — their own people broke it, to keep him from swallowing the worldsoul.

summary: Kezan is the goblins' home island in the South Seas, a tropical volcanic rock carved into trade districts by the trade princes and paved wherever paving could be sold. Its real capital is Undermine, a sprawl of tunnels, vaults and lava tubes running through Mount Kajaro beneath it. The volcano erupted during the Cataclysm and drove the Bilgewater Cartel off the island for good; only the goblin starting experience is played here, and the survivors now live in Azshara.
history: Goblins reached Kezan roughly ten thousand years ago, after the Sundering. The Zandalari came for the kaja'mite beneath the island, found more of it than they could ever need, and put the goblins to work in the mines instead of digging themselves; breathing the ore dust woke an intelligence the goblins had long forgotten they had. A century before the Dark Portal opened they came out of the tunnels armed with things the trolls had no answer to and took the island. Freedom went straight into feuding, the feuds hardened into cartels, and the cartels made a truce and competed over money instead. When the kaja'mite ran out and the inventions started failing, trade was what was left. Then Deathwing's return set Mount Kajaro off and the harbours went under.

summary: Korthia is an old realm of the Shadowlands that was deliberately hidden and is no longer hidden. The Jailer's chains hauled it out of the In-Between and set it down in the southeast of the Maw, and his Mawsworn have been digging through its vaults ever since for whatever the First Ones left in them. Its attendants survived the journey, the covenants landed an army behind them under Death's Advance, and both sides are now racing the other to the relics.
history: Korthia was put in the In-Between on purpose, by people who wanted what it held kept away from exactly the sort of hands that eventually came for it. A fatescribe ran the place and an archivist kept its records, working a lodestaff that can find any artefact if the Netherstar is feeding it. The Primus, knowing what was coming for him, left his sigil in the vaults here before the Jailer took him. Dragging the realm into the Maw tore the fabric of the Shadowlands where it had been. Death's Advance crossed over to hold it, the surviving scholars organised into the Archivists' Codex, and Roh-Suir was made archivist in the middle of it.

summary: The Krasarang Wilds are the jungle along Pandaria's southern coast: heavy air, vine-covered ruins, and saurok who have held the undergrowth since they turned on the mogu who made them. Chi-Ji's Temple of the Red Crane stands inland, and the Sha of Despair is loose from its bindings there. Since the war reached the continent the beaches have been a front line, Lion's Landing for the Alliance and Domination Point for the Horde, with the Anglers fishing off the coast between them.
history: This was the outer edge of the mogu empire, and the edge is where it split. The saurok the mogu had built as soldiers rebelled here, killed Emperor Dojan II, and vanished into undergrowth they hold to this day. Long afterwards, with the world beyond the mists assumed destroyed, Liu Lang put to sea from the beach on a young turtle to check; a statue on the sand marks it. Then visions of a light in the jungle drew two expeditions inland — night elves after a mogu spring said to grant endless life, which turned out only to move it from one body to another, and Sunwalker Dezco's tauren, who buried his wife here. Behind them the Sha of Despair came out of the Temple of the Red Crane and took Chi-Ji himself.

summary: Krokuun is the surface of Argus, and the first ground Azeroth's armies set foot on when they took the war to the Legion's home world. What were eredar cities and groves is now black soil, petrified trees and demonic machinery growing out of the rock like more rock. The Army of the Light's crashed Xenedar lies here, the Broken survivors shelter at Krokul Hovel, and the fortified city of Nath'raxas Hold looks down on all of it.
history: Argus was the eredar's own world and this was its countryside. When Sargeras made his offer, Kil'jaeden and Archimonde accepted it and Velen fled with those who would follow, leaving the rest to be remade as the man'ari. The eredar who kept neither the Light nor the fel were broken by the planet's ruin and became the Krokul, worked as slaves in their own hills. The Army of the Light fought on from its dimensional ship for millennia. When the Vindicaar finally brought champions of Azeroth down at Darkfall Ridge they freed those slaves, made common cause with Chieftain Hatuun's people and pushed inland to Nath'raxas Hold, with Kil'jaeden's wrecked ship still burning behind them.
