summary: Kun-Lai Summit is northern Pandaria: dry autumn plains in the south climbing into the coldest mountains on the continent, with Mount Neverest over everything. Xuen's Temple of the White Tiger and the Shado-Pan's monastery are both up here and both are in trouble — yaungol driven out of Townlong have burned their way across the farmland, and the sha have risen inside the monastery itself. On the northern coast a Zandalari fleet has landed and made common cause with the mogu again.
history: The mountains are titan work shaped by mogu hands, and mogu clans fought over them long before the Thunder King united anyone. Lei Shen offered the summit's people their freedom on a single duel; Xuen took it, fought him for thirty days and nights, lost, and was chained on Mount Neverest to watch the empire rise. Generations later the pandaren Kang climbed up and found him still willing to teach. Ten thousand quiet years followed the revolution. Then both armies carried their wounded to Binan for its healers, yaungol crossed the wall ahead of the mantid and burned Westwind Rest, and Xuen — having tested the outsiders and opened the road to the Vale — sent Taran Zhu home angry enough to wake the sha under his own monastery.

summary: Loch Modan is dwarf country east of Dun Morogh, grey hills lightly wooded in pine and birch around the basin the loch used to fill. The Stonewrought Dam broke when Deathwing came up through Azeroth and the water drained out of it, leaving mudflats, islands that are no longer islands and Second War siege engines lying where they sank. Thelsamar is the town, Ironband's excavation is why the troggs are out of the ground, and Mo'grosh ogres, kobolds and Bluegill murlocs share what the loch left behind.
history: The dwarves dammed the valley and made the loch, and the Stonewrought Dam that held it was reckoned to have no equal anywhere on Azeroth. When the Horde came for Khaz Modan's ore and oil in the Second War it overran this valley too, and the broken catapults and ballistae lying about the basin are from that campaign; Kilrogg Deadeye's clan was left behind to hold the region and was hunted out of it when the Alliance swept south, which gave Ironforge the ground back. Digging under the hills for titan relics brought the troggs up instead, and they have camped in the mountains ever since, alongside the Mo'grosh ogres in the northeast. Then Deathwing burst out of the earth, cracked the dam and emptied the loch, which is why the map no longer matches anyone's memory of it.

summary: Maldraxxus is the Shadowlands' army, and looks it: a blighted country of bone, iron and fungus where the ground itself seems to take an interest in what walks on it. Souls too stubborn to yield are sent here, made over into undead soldiers, and set against whatever threatens the realms of death from outside. The Primus who founded the place has gone missing, and the five houses that answered to him have turned their strength on each other.
history: Necromancy was invented here, and every plague and lich Azeroth has suffered traces back to it — the Lich King's power was Maldraxxian work. The Primus built five houses to hold the realm's strength and set them competing so that only the strongest rose, which worked for as long as somebody stood above them. Then he left for the Maw and did not come back. Without him the competition became a war: the House of Eyes was wiped out and the House of Plagues rotted from within, the Chosen lost their margrave, and the House of Constructs and the sorcerers of the House of Rituals were quietly working for the Jailer the whole time. Draka's rise from the Theater of Pain is what put the houses back together.

summary: Mechagon is a small island northwest of Kul Tiras, green on the surface and hollowed out underneath by the gnomish city its king spent four centuries building. Its people replaced their own flesh with machinery to stop growing old, and then split over how far that should go: Prince Erazmin's Rustbolt Resistance against King Mechagon's Arcforged. Scrapbone troggs hold the northern hills and the junk of the whole project litters the coast.
history: Mimiron kept a vault of titan work on this island long before anyone settled it, and vrykul and tortollan left traces here before the gnomes did. Four hundred years ago the king of Gnomeregan took his followers out to look for a land of machines, told nobody where he was going, and passed into legend at home. He found it, claimed it, and had Mechagon City dug out beneath the surface, where his gnomes began trading flesh for parts. His last project was the Mechoriginator, a machine meant to strip the Curse of Flesh from every titan creation whether it wanted that or not. His son's attempt to stop him was betrayed to him, and the civil war that followed brought the Alliance and Horde in on the prince's side.

summary: Moonglade is a walled-in vale in northern Kalimdor that nothing has been allowed to spoil: old forest, mounds full of sleeping druids, and Lake Elune'ara in the middle of it with Nighthaven on the shore. It is the Cenarion Circle's home and neutral ground — night elf and tauren druids train here side by side, and the Moonglade Wardens stop anyone who tries to bring a war into it. The only way in on foot is the Timbermaw tunnel through the southwestern mountains, which is why most people arrive some other way.
history: Cenarius lived here in the age of the War of the Ancients, and it was here that Malfurion brought Tyrande and Illidan to ask the demigod for help against the Legion. After the Sundering the keepers of the grove and the dryads came out of this valley into the wider world, and during the War of the Satyr Malfurion gathered druids here and founded the Cenarion Circle. In the Third War Tichondrius sent the Scourge at the barrow dens to reach Malfurion's sleeping body; Tyrande recovered the Horn of Cenarius and woke him instead. Afterwards the vale opened to druids of every race under Keeper Remulos, and the Nightmare found a way into one wing of the dens.

summary: Mount Hyjal is the sacred peak of northern Kalimdor, crowned by the World Tree Nordrassil and the second Well of Eternity beneath it. It is druid country: the Cenarion Circle and the Guardians of Hyjal keep the shrines to the Ancients here, alongside the night elves of Nordrassil and the green dragonflight that has watched the mountain since the world was ordered. The forest is still visibly recovering from the fire that came up out of the Firelands during the Cataclysm.
history: Freya bound her Wild Gods' spirits to the Emerald Dream here and left Ysera's flight guarding them. Dark trolls lived in caverns under it and Azshara's empire never came up the slope. When the first Well of Eternity imploded and broke the world, Hyjal endured and the survivors climbed to it; Illidan poured a second Well on the summit from stolen vials, and the kaldorei planted Nordrassil over it with three Aspects' blessing and sealed its maker into one of the barrow dens beneath the mountain. Archimonde came for that Well in the Third War and the wisps destroyed him, taking night elven immortality with him. Deathwing tore the Firelands open on the summit and Ragnaros came up through it; the druids called the Wild Gods back to the mountain, Cenarius among them, then carried the war down into the fire and killed him in his own hall. The Aspects healed Nordrassil afterwards.

summary: Mulgore is the tauren's valley: green rolling grassland walled in by mountains on every side, with one pass out to the east that the Great Gate now closes. Thunder Bluff stands on mesas hundreds of feet above the plain in the north, Bloodhoof Village sits on Stonebull Lake in the middle, and Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa is where young tauren are trained. It is pastoral rather than peaceful — Bristleback quilboar press out of Brambleblade Ravine, Palemane gnolls hold the western caves, Windfury harpies the far north, and the Venture Company and the Grimtotem both go after the water.
history: This valley is remembered as the tauren's oldest home, and they were driven out of it into centuries of nomadic wandering and running war with the centaur. Cairne Bloodhoof met Thrall's orcs when they landed on Kalimdor, and with their help took the plains back and raised Thunder Bluff on the mesas, a city open to every tauren tribe. The scattered tribes gathered under him there. After the war against the Lich King, Garrosh Hellscream killed Cairne in a duel that Magatha Grimtotem had poisoned, and the Grimtotem seized Thunder Bluff before the tauren retook it; Baine rules from his father's place now. Then the Cataclysm roused the earth spirits under the dwarven dig and let the quilboar loose across Red Cloud Mesa.

summary: Nagrand is the windswept west of Draenor: open plains under impossible arches of floating rock, with the crystal mountain of Oshu'gun at the centre and the elements stirring at the Throne of the Elements. Seafaring ogres of the Gorian Empire hold the south from Highmaul, where Imperator Mar'gok rules what is left of their empire. The Warsong and Burning Blade clans hold the east for the Iron Horde out of Grommashar and Hallvalor, and the Black Market has moved its business into the Ring of Blood.
history: The giant Grond's head came to rest here, and the elementals born out of his remains never left it; the orcs cut a temple into the skull and called the place the Throne of the Elements, and shamanism began there. Gorian sorcerers blew that temple apart trying to take the power for themselves, and the war it provoked ended with the elements swallowing the ogre capital whole. Nagrand — "land of winds" — was the clans' common ground afterwards: twice a year they gathered beneath Oshu'gun for the Kosh'harg and set their feuds down. The Warsong later claimed the plains outright and paid in ogre raids, one of which killed Grommash Hellscream's mate Golka. At Highmaul a slave revolt cost the emperor his head to Kargath Bladefist; Mar'gok's diminished empire now keeps an uneasy bargain with the Iron Horde.

summary: Nagrand is the green heart of Outland, a plateau of grassland, lakes and floating islands that the fel corruption which shattered the rest of Draenor barely touched. It is the ancestral home of the orcs and the birthplace of their shamanism, and today it is shared by the uncorrupted Mag'har and the Broken draenei of the Kurenai. Its centre is Halaa, a plateau town that changes hands between the Alliance and the Horde as often as either can hold it.
history: Grond's head fell here, and the elemental spirits that first took shape in his remains never left it. Mystics out of Shadowmoon Valley found them, named the place the Throne of the Elements and cut a temple into the skull, which is where shamanism began. It was there that Gul'dan drained the four elemental furies and traded the elements for fel. Garadar was a quarantine camp for orcs dying of his red pox, which is why nobody penned in it drank Mannoroth's blood and the Mag'har are uncorrupted still. Draenor shattered; Nagrand largely survived. Thrall came to Garadar generations later, met the grandmother he had never known and took Garrosh Hellscream home with him. He returned before the Cataclysm to be trained by Aggra, and the furies told him Azeroth's elements sounded as Draenor's had before it came apart.

summary: Nazjatar is the naga capital, sunk in a trench under the Great Sea where the night elf city of Zin-Azshari once stood. Queen Azshara pulled the water back off it, leaving a drowned landscape walled in by standing waterfalls, with the Eternal Palace at its heart. The Alliance and Horde fleets she wrecked here are stranded among makrura, sea giants and the naga's slaves, and have thrown in with the escaped Unshackled and the Waveblade Ankoan to survive.
history: When the Well of Eternity collapsed and the Highborne who followed Azshara were reshaped into naga, they went down to where their old capital had drowned and built a new one over it. Azshara took the drowned Zin-Azshari into it and told her people their empire beneath the sea would outgrow anything the night elves had held. For ten thousand years almost nobody saw it. Then Sylvanas sent a fleet out from Zuldazar following Xal'atath's blade, Jaina's ships chased it, and Azshara used the Tidestone of Golganneth to open the sea and drop both fleets onto her reefs. Her masters wanted her prisoners; her prisoners eventually reached the palace and put her down, which left the naga to fracture among themselves.

summary: Nazmir is the swamp filling the northeast of Zandalar, standing water and insects and the broken stonework of temples the jungle has half swallowed. The blood trolls hold it now, worshipping the Old God G'huun as a loa and working to break the last titan disc that keeps him sealed under Uldir. Bwonsamdi still keeps his Necropolis here, and Zandalari mothers still use the swamp to frighten their children.
history: This was the first home of troll civilisation, and the first king led his people south out of it to found Zuldazar because of what was buried underneath. The titans had built a facility here to study the Old Gods and had accidentally made one of their own, and the seal on it has been the region's whole story since. Nazmir stayed a place of worship for the loa of death for centuries afterwards, with temples at the Necropolis and the Terrace of Sorrows, until heretics began killing and corrupting the faithful and became the blood trolls. In the Fourth War Talanji brought allies into the swamp against them, and G'huun was put down inside Uldir rather than merely sealed again.

summary: Netherstorm is the northeastern edge of Outland, seven large islands and thousands of smaller rocks hanging in a violet arcane storm where the Twisting Nether leaks through into the world. Nothing grows on the purple bedrock except inside the ethereals' eco-domes, which is why the Consortium's Stormspire is a jungle under glass in the middle of a magical desert. Goblins run Area 52 and are building a rocket, Kael'thas's Sunfury blood elves hold Tempest Keep and the manaforges, the Burning Legion works its forge bases in between, and Kirin'Var Village stands empty except for its ghosts.
history: Before the sundering this was Farahlon, forest and open range on the Devouring Sea, grown from the corpse of the sporemound Botaan and held by the Primals. Its isolation kept it clear of fel magic longest, until Kilrogg Deadeye ferried the Bleeding Hollow across on ogre-built ships and warlocks burned the forests with power leeched from the botani. The Kirin Tor of the Alliance Expedition built Kirin'Var Village here. Ner'zhul's portals shattered the island into the floating shards it is now. The naaru arrived for that same reason, riding Tempest Keep in through borders the Nether had worn thin; A'dal went on to Shattrath and Kael'thas took what was left, stripping it for parts and raising five manaforges that pulled the land apart faster. Velen's draenei raided the Keep for one wing and flew it to Azeroth as the Exodar.

summary: The Northern Barrens is the upper half of the old Barrens savanna, dry veld dotted with scrub, hills and three oases, and it is the road country that ties Orgrimmar to the rest of Kalimdor. The Crossroads sits where the north-south and east-west roads meet and is the busiest Horde town in central Kalimdor; the goblin port of Ratchet takes anyone's coin on the eastern shore, and the Mor'shan Rampart guards the northern approach from Ashenvale. Its southern edge is the Great Divide, the magma-filled gorge Deathwing left, which is why the zone has a compass point in its name at all.
history: This was quilboar and centaur range long before the Horde crossed the Southfury, and the orcs took it as their road: the Crossroads was raised at the junction, Grol'dom and the other farms behind it, and generations of young Horde soldiers cut their teeth on Razormane and Witchwing raiders. Beneath the oasis to the south the druid Naralex tried to dream the Barrens green again and touched the Emerald Nightmare instead, which is what the Wailing Caverns are. Deathwing's flight tore the gorge across the middle and left the northern half alone with its trade routes. Kor'kron work camps went up here during the rebellion against Garrosh, the Legion picked it as an invasion point and lost, and the Scourge came back through during Death Rising.

summary: Northern Stranglethorn is the upper half of the vale, dense tropical jungle running from the Duskwood border down to the channel the Cataclysm tore through the middle of the region. Nobody owns it: the Gurubashi hold Zul'Gurub, the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter hold the ruins between, the Horde moves supplies through Grom'gol and the Alliance answers from Fort Livingston and the Rebel Camp. The Venture Company strips whatever it can carry, Kurzen's old expedition has gone feral in its own compound, and Nesingwary's safari shoots the rest.
history: The vale was the heart of the Gurubashi Empire, which held a great stretch of the southern continent until its trolls turned on the loa Hakkar and broke themselves doing it, some fifteen centuries before the Dark Portal. The survivors split into Bloodscalp, Skullsplitter and the rest and began fighting over the jungle at once; the Darkspear were driven out altogether and only came back generations later, founding Bambala. Stormwind's expansion down the coast brought war back to the vale: Prince Llane, Lothar and Medivh came in to kill the Gurubashi leadership, the trolls marched on the capital in answer, and Medivh burned their army off the field at its gates. The Bleeding Hollow tried the jungle next in the First War and were bled white in it until Blackhand recalled them. The Shattering split the vale in two.

summary: The Ohn'ahran Plains are open grassland in the middle of the Dragon Isles, shared between the green dragonflight in the wooded groves and the Maruuk Centaur out on the grass. They are named for Ohn'ahra, the eagle Wild God who brought the centaur here, and the four clans still order themselves around her — mystics at the springs, hunters on the range, keepers of the old ways, and a caravan that never stops moving. The exception is Clan Nokhud, which took the Primalists' offer and turned on everyone else.
history: Ohn'ahra led Maruuk and Teera's people to these plains, where they promptly went to war with the green flight over them. Neither side could win, so they divided the land instead: dragons in the groves, centaur on the open ground. That settlement outlived the settlers. The Sundering drained the isles, the flights withdrew, and the centaur were left to themselves for ten thousand years — long enough to build a whole culture out of what had been a bargain, with clans, khans and a burial ground for their ancestors. It held until the Nokhud, newest of the great clans and the one with the largest army, took power from the Primal Incarnates' followers and set about the others.

summary: Orgrimmar is the Horde's capital, a walled warren of valleys cut into the canyons of northern Durotar and named for Orgrim Doomhammer. Grommash Hold at its centre was the warchief's seat and is now the Horde Council's, the office having been abolished rather than passed on. Each people that joined the Horde has taken a quarter of it — tauren in the Valley of Wisdom, Darkspear in the Valley of Spirits, goblins in the slums, everyone else through the embassy by the gate.
history: Thrall's people came ashore after Mount Hyjal and raised a fortified city in a few short years, with goblin, tauren and troll hands helping and Rexxar fighting off everything in Durotar that objected. It was built to be defended, its rear wall the mountain itself. The Scourge came at the gates twice; Sylvanas sheltered here after the Wrathgate. When Thrall left for Nagrand he handed the Horde to Garrosh Hellscream, who tore the city down and rebuilt it in iron and spikes, less flammable and far more warlike, with the races pushed into separate valleys. That ended in the siege that dragged him out of a bunker under Ragefire Chasm, and after one more war the Horde stopped appointing warchiefs at all.

summary: Oribos is the first thing a soul sees after dying: a ringed city of strange metal at the centre of the Shadowlands, built by the First Ones, where the Arbiter judged every arrival and sent them on to the afterlife that fit them. Souls still pour up its central pillar, but for a long stretch they went nowhere except the Maw, because the Arbiter had gone dark. Attendants run the city, brokers run the trade, and Alliance and Horde are both admitted on the strict condition they leave the war outside.
history: The city predates anyone's memory of it, and the brokers who make their living inside it cannot find its ore anywhere else — one of them calls the place an ancient engine, which is closer to the truth than a description. For as long as there had been mortal souls the Arbiter sat in the Crucible at its crown and sorted every one of them. Then she was struck down, the sorting stopped, and everything that died fell into the Maw while the other realms starved for the anima those souls carried. Oribos became a war camp for the living: the covenants' representatives, both factions' leaders and the former Lich King all working out of the Enclave. Pelagos took up the judgement afterwards.

summary: The Redridge Mountains are green valley country east of Elwynn: elms, red canyon walls and the long water of Lake Everstill, with the town of Lakeshire on its western shore and the Three Corners crossroads in the southwest. Stonewatch Keep guards the eastern heights, held for years by Blackrock orcs and taken back with the help of the reformed Bravo Company. The Lakeridge Highway between them is still a road nobody walks alone, worked by Shadowhide gnolls, murlocs and orc camps.
history: The range is the spine of the continent, and the Dragon Soul lay warded beneath it for ten thousand years, kept by the red dragon Orastrasz until Deathwing drew the Dragonmaw here in dreams and they killed him for it. Two centuries before the Dark Portal, Thaurissan's summoning of Ragnaros raised Blackrock Mountain and burned the northern reaches into ash, leaving Redridge only its southern half. In the First War the orcs took Lakeshire and everything around it — Lothar nearly killed Blackhand in an ambush here first — and the beaten Horde fell back on these valleys after its first assault on Stormwind failed. The humans returned to rebuild, the Blackrock clan returned too and seized Stonewatch with the warlock Morganth, and after the Cataclysm the Dark Horde came again behind the dragon Darkblaze.

summary: Revendreth is where the Arbiter sends souls too proud or too flawed for anywhere else, and nobody arrives here glad of it. The venthyr break that pride out of them by torment, because the only thing on the far side of failure is the Maw. It is a country of red stone and gothic spires under permanent gloom, except where the Light has burned through the cloud and scorched the ground — and those patches are where souls that cannot bear it get chained.
history: Sire Denathrius made this realm and the Court of Harvesters that runs it, each harvester embodying a sin and answerable for wringing it out of the souls in their care. Redemption was the point, and the anima recovered along the way was Revendreth's tithe to the rest of the Shadowlands. Denathrius stopped paying it. He was pouring the realm's anima into the Maw for the Jailer, having been the first of the nathrezim long before he was anyone's master, and the drought that starved every other realm started at his own table. Prince Renathal saw it, said so, and was thrown out of the castle for it; his rebellion works out of Sinfall.

summary: The Searing Gorge is the northern half of the same disaster that made the Burning Steppes: a burnt valley in southern Khaz Modan below Blackrock Mountain, worked end to end by the Dark Iron clan. The Cauldron is the enormous excavation at its centre, ringed by digging machines with the Slag Pit sunk underneath, and most of the labour in it is not volunteered. On the cliffs above sit the Thorium Brotherhood at Thorium Point, Dark Irons who left the clan and now watch what it does.
history: Some two and a half centuries ago this was a green valley in the Redridge range. Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan and seven of his most powerful dwarves called on the old thing sleeping beneath the world to break the War of the Three Hammers in their favour, and what answered was Ragnaros; Blackrock Mountain erupted out of the ridge, the Dark Iron capital was reduced to rubble, and the valley north of it was left as it now stands. The clan rebuilt under the mountain and turned the blackened ground into a mining concern, cutting the Cauldron with captive labour. The Brotherhood split off and settled the rim, and Stonewrought Pass to Loch Modan stayed sealed for years until the Cataclysm forced it open.

summary: Shadowmoon Valley is the south-eastern corner of Draenor and the draenei heartland: a green valley under permanent night, lit by a moon bright enough to stand in for the sun. The temple of Karabor holds the coast, Elodor feeds the valley and seats the Council of Exarchs, and Velen himself is here. Against that, the Shadowmoon orcs have turned to the void in the fortress above their burial grounds and the Iron Horde is striking the shore, while the Alliance expedition digs in at Lunarfall.
history: Orcs came out of Gorgrond some eight centuries ago and named themselves for this valley. Their mystics found the Throne of the Elements, gave orcish shamanism its shape and called the first Kosh'harg, and their chieftains outlawed the Dark Star over the slopes after it shattered the minds of everyone who reached for it. The draenei then made the valley the centre of their faith, raising Karabor on the coast to steady a land their crash had wrecked, with Elodor, Embaari and the observatory at Teluuna behind it. Now Ner'zhul has turned from the ancestors to the void; his clan fills Anguish Fortress with draenei captives and spends their deaths calling void things into the world, and those who refused — Rulkan among them — fled up Mount Kra'gor. In the timeline that produced Outland, Karabor became the Black Temple.

summary: Shadowmoon Valley is the southeastern corner of Outland and the most thoroughly ruined ground in it: black rock and ash under a yellow-green sky, green lava running off the volcano at its centre, and infernals falling out of the clouds without pause. The Black Temple stands on the coast, held in turn by the Shadow Council, a pit lord, Illidan Stormrage and finally Akama's Broken. Around it are Legion holdings, Dragonmaw fel orcs breaking nether drakes to the saddle, Coilskar naga, and small camps of everybody else — Aldor, Scryers, Wildhammer dwarves and the Horde — all here because of what is in the temple.
history: The valley was a moor under permanent night, lit by two moons. Orcs out of Gorgrond settled it, took its name and charted its stars. The draenei crash-landed afterwards; their vessel ejected the darkened naaru K'ara as the Dark Star, whose power the Shadowmoon chieftain forbade for what it did to minds that touched it. The draenei raised the Temple of Karabor on the coast, and Gul'dan shattered the firelord Cyrukh outside it, leaving the Hand of Gul'dan. The Shadow Council then called K'ara's void down on Karabor, killing hundreds and making the Black Temple. Ner'zhul's ritual on its highest tower tore the world apart. Magtheridon held the ruin until Illidan Stormrage took it from him; Akama turned on Illidan at the end and freed Maiev Shadowsong, who carried his body and his demon hunters back to Azeroth in crystal.

summary: Shattrath is the one place in Outland that is not a battlefield: a terraced sanctuary in northwestern Terokkar Forest ruled by the naaru of the Sha'tar from the Terrace of Light, open to Alliance and Horde alike on the condition that neither brings the war inside. Two orders share it badly — the draenei priesthood of the Aldor on one rise, the blood elf defectors of the Scryers on the other, each courting A'dal's favour at the other's expense. Below them the Lower City holds everyone the broken world displaced.
history: The draenei founded it roughly two centuries before the Dark Portal on the wreck of Goria, the ogre capital the elements swallowed at the orcs' asking; the ruins lay unclaimed because nobody native would go near them. Exarch Hataaru designed what replaced them, the finest thing the draenei built on Draenor. A century later Imperator Hok'lon came to take the site back and lost his generals and his life to Akama, Maraad and Nobundo; no ogre tried the walls again. Then the orcs came. With Karabor lost the draenei chose to stand here as a decoy; Velen blessed everyone who stayed and led the civilians out to Telredor. Plague bombs came over the walls and infernals fell inside them, and the ruins sat dark for years until Aldor priests crept back into a temple and their rites drew A'dal in. Under the Sha'tar the refuge became a base as well: the naaru Xi'ri led its forces into Shadowmoon Valley and into the storming of the Black Temple, and when Kael'thas began drawing Kil'jaeden through the Sunwell, A'dal's answer was to put the Aldor and the Scryers — two orders that will not willingly share a stair — into a single army. That was the Shattered Sun Offensive, and it sailed from here to Quel'Danas to take the island back.

summary: Sholazar Basin is a hot, humid jungle sunk into the middle of an arctic continent, and none of it is natural: a ring of titan pillars around the basin floor pours life magic into the air, holding the climate steady and the Scourge out. It is Freya's nursery, and the wildlife in it is larger and stranger than anything outside. Two tribes are at each other's throats across it — the wolvar of the Frenzyheart and the gorlocs who call themselves the Oracles — while Hemet Nesingwary's safari shoots its way through the middle and the Scourge press in through a gap in the north.
history: Freya shaped the basin as one of three sites where the Well of Eternity's energies had gathered, the others being Un'Goro Crater and the Vale of Eternal Blossoms, and all three were run as experiments in life. Wild Gods came out of these cradles. The earliest work was housed at Wintergrasp and the most promising of it was moved here. During the war against the Lich King, the Cult of the Damned brought down the Lifeblood Pillar in the east; the snows of Icecrown poured through the breach as the Avalanche, and the blighted Lost Lands spread out beneath it. Freya had left a failsafe — an Avatar of herself — which has been holding the line there ever since, with help.

summary: Silithus is the southwestern corner of Kalimdor and it is no longer really a desert: Sargeras drove his sword into it and most of the zone is now the Wound, a torn crater with the world-soul's blood pooling at the bottom of it and Azerite crystallising out of the rock. Magni Bronzebeard works the site with the Cenarion Circle and the Earthen Ring beside him, and the Horde mines the same seams from the ruins of Southwind Village. South of all that the old Silithus is still there — the Scarab Wall, the gates of Ahn'Qiraj, silithid hives, and the Cenarion Circle holding its keep.
history: Highkeeper Ra raised Ahn'Qiraj over the pit C'Thun was entombed in and posted anubisath giants above it. Ages later the aqir, underground since the trolls broke their empire, crept into the empty fortress, and the Old God reworked them into the qiraji. Nobody remembered they were there until Fandral Staghelm's druids came to green the desert and his son Valstan walked in. The War of the Shifting Sands cost Valstan his life and ended with the swarm walled in rather than killed. Millennia later it came out again; Anachronos named C'Thun as the cause, both factions put Varok Saurfang over one army, and they reforged the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, opened the wall themselves and killed the Old God underneath it. Then Sargeras's blade came down, and everything since has been about the bleeding.

summary: Silvermoon is the capital of Quel'Thalas and the blood elves' own city, white stone under crimson banners in the north of Eversong Woods, guarding the road to the Sunwell. Lor'themar Theron rules as regent lord for a dynasty with no heir left, advised by Grand Magister Rommath and Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing. Only the eastern half is a city: the Dead Scar still cuts past it, and the western districts beyond are ruins full of Wretched and arcane constructs that never stopped working.
history: Highborne exiles under Dath'Remar Sunstrider crossed the sea about sixty-eight centuries before the Dark Portal, poured a stolen measure of the Well of Eternity into a new one, and raised a capital on its power — on ground the Amani held sacred, which bought them an enemy for the rest of their history. The Troll Wars made allies of them and Arathor, and a Sunwell-fed shield kept invaders out for seven thousand years. Gul'dan broke that shield in the Second War by turning the elves' own runestones against it, and still the siege failed. What did not fail was Arthas: he cut a scar the length of the kingdom, took the city and fouled the Sunwell. The magisters rebuilt with borrowed fel until Quel'Danas gave the well back.

summary: Silverpine is a tall, quiet pine forest down Lordaeron's western coast, mist on the needles and abandoned farms and mine shafts scattered through it. The Forsaken hold the north from the Sepulcher and their command posts, and used the southern woods as the staging ground for the invasion of Gilneas; the Bloodfang worgen and the Gilneas Liberation Front dispute everything below that, and Shadowfang Keep is now the pack's. Fenris Isle sits out in Lordamere Lake, Pyrewood and Ambermill were Gilnean towns before the Greymane Wall cut them off, and ettins have wandered up from the south since it fell.
history: Pyrewood and Ambermill belonged to Gilneas until the Greymane Wall shut the kingdom away. The great road through these pines was the way to the capital, and Lothar brought Stormwind's refugees up it after the First War. The Scourge pushed through the forest during the Third War and stalled at that wall; Genn Greymane sent his soldiers out and watched them raised as undead, then had Archmage Arugal pull worgen out of the Emerald Dream to fight in their place. The curse got into the living, Gilneas abandoned Silverpine trying to contain it, and Arugal went mad with guilt and took Shadowfang Keep for himself and the beasts he called his children. With Lordaeron gone and Dalaran busy rebuilding, nobody was left holding the woods, so the Forsaken took them — and later marched on Gilneas from them. Sylvanas paid for that campaign with val'kyr, raising three dead Gilnean lords who had never accepted a wolf for a king; once the worgen had been pushed back over the border, Godfrey shot her in the back and ran for Shadowfang Keep with the other two, and it took her own val'kyr to raise her again.

summary: Siren Isle is a storm-battered rock in the Great Sea that Kul Tiras mined for azerite during the Fourth War, until everyone who worked it stopped being there. A goblin salvage crew found it again, along with a crystal at its heart that sings, and the Hallowfall Arathi, the earthen of Dornogal and Gazlowe's Greasemonkeys have thrown in together to work out what it is — the Arathi call it Lorandel and say it is Beledar's twin. Bloodwake vrykul, Darktide naga and Bilge Rat pirates are all trying to take the island off them.
history: The vrykul knew this place as Cyrandall. Twenty thousand years ago the iron vrykul Cyrce brought the Sturmvyn clan here to sit out the Winterskorn War, and they named the place the Cradle of Hymosul and lived on it for ten thousand years. Then the Sundering, and after it the naga, who came out of the water in numbers the clan could not fight — Cyrce ordered a retreat into a vault beneath the island and the door shut on them. Nothing much happened for a long age afterwards except a Kul Tiran azerite dig, and everyone on that vanished too. In 42 ADP a goblin salvage team put in, heard the crystal, and the whole of Khaz Algar came looking.

summary: The Southern Barrens is what the lower half of the savanna became after Deathwing split it off: a war zone with a bottleneck in the middle of it. Desolation Hold and Fort Triumph face each other across the Battlescar, the Alliance pushing inland from the coast and the Horde trying to shut the pass and cut Theramore off by land. North of the fighting the Overgrowth has swallowed the plains in jungle that kills, the tauren have sealed Mulgore behind the Great Gate, and the quilboar hold everything south down to Razorfen Kraul.
history: Camp Taurajo was the Horde's waystation on the southern road and the Bael Modan dwarves dug at the old titan works nearby, and that was most of what happened here until Deathwing's gorge cut the region loose from the north. General Hawthorne burned Taurajo in the aftermath and earned a name the Horde still uses for him; the tauren answered by walling off Mulgore. Both sides then dug in either side of the Battlescar for the pass itself. Garrosh razed Northwatch Hold and then Fort Triumph on his march to Theramore, and the Alliance later took Northwatch back. The Fourth War hit every holding in the region, and since the armistice the lines have simply stopped moving.

summary: Spires of Arak is southern Draenor: a forest under the broken stumps of what was once a single enormous spire. The winged arakkoa rule from Skyreach at the top of the tallest of them and treat their wingless kin as refuse, while the outcasts keep to the shade below. Round the edges the Shattered Hand clan hunts arakkoa for sport from Bladefist Hold, goblins run a gearworks on the coast, and both Azerothian factions have put ships ashore.
history: Arak was one vast spire, and the arakkoa on it built the Apexis empire around it — until their priests and their sorcerers fell out over who could read the empire's knowledge, and the sabotaged Breath of Rukhmar blew the mountain into the ridges the zone now carries as a name. What grew back was a theocracy. Heretics were thrown into Sethekk Hollow, where the blood of the dead wind serpent Sethe twisted them into flightless outcasts, and King Terokk — who built Skyreach and tried to take the priests' power off them — went into those pools himself. Kargath Bladefist finished the argument for both sides: he bought the outcasts' help to sabotage Skyreach's solar weapon, slaughtered the winged, then forced the survivors into the pools as well. Of all of it, only Skettis survived into Outland.

summary: The Stonetalon Mountains are the wooded range between Ashenvale and Desolace, evergreen at the top and thinning to bare rock below, and they are where night elf and tauren country have always met. Years of logging by the Venture Company and then by both war machines have stripped Windshear Crag down to soot and oiled water, Krom'gar Fortress sits above the valley the Horde is fighting for, and the Charred Vale in the west is a burnt plain of fire elementals and black dragons. Sun Rock Retreat holds the centre for the tauren, Malaka'jin the south for the Darkspear, and the Alliance works out of Windshear Hold and Farwatcher's Glen.
history: Elune blessed a fountain in these mountains in the ancient world, and the first tauren to settle them carried burning totems to the highest peaks in honour of An'she. Stonetalon Peak was sacred to night elf and tauren alike and was the home of the Oracle. During the Third War the harpies fouled Elune's fountain; Thrall and Cairne Bloodhoof took a glyph from the centaur to cleanse it and freed the captive wyverns that carried them up to the peak, where Horde and Alliance briefly stood together against the Legion. Goblin logging and mining then stripped the range and the spirits cried out over it. After the Cataclysm the peak came under Old God attack, and Overlord Krom'gar destroyed a grove of druid students on a suspicion.

summary: Stormheim is the eastern end of the Broken Isles: fjords, ravines and amber woods cut out of the rock by the sea, covered in vrykul monuments. The vrykul here live between two afterlives that are both directly overhead — Odyn's Halls of Valor in the clouds and Helya's Helheim under the water — and the clans are split over which one they serve. The Legion's bargain has already taken the Tideskorn, and the Alliance and Horde have landed on the same coast looking for the Aegis of Aggramar.
history: The vrykul took this land from Highborne occupants under King Magnar Icebreaker, only for Helya's followers to murder Magnar and his son in the hour of their victory. Millennia later, with the Halls of Valor hanging in the sky as Odyn's prison, vrykul crossed from Northrend in numbers to live beneath them and hope for a place among the Valarjar; Helya's kvaldir have been picking off their dead ever since. When the Legion returned, Prince Skovald of the Tideskorn made a pact with the demons, killed his father, then his brothers, then his mother, and made himself God-King with fel-corrupted Felskorn at his back. The two Azerothian factions arrived, and promptly fought each other.

summary: Stormsong Valley is the northern end of Kul Tiras, green rolling farmland between two mountain ranges, reached from the rest of the island only through the Highland Pass. It grows most of the kingdom's food and builds most of its ships, which the tidesages of House Stormsong bless before they ever touch water. The house has since sold itself to Azshara, the shipyards have stopped, quilboar press in from the south and the Horde has cut a camp out of the northern woods, so the militia of Storm's Wake holds what is left from Brennadam.
history: The valley took its name from the family that settled it, and the tidesages that the last lord's father brought with him made it the religious heart of a kingdom already devoted to the sea. Everything here bent toward one purpose: grain from the hills, timber floated down the Twin Rivers, hulls laid at Mariner's Strand and each one consecrated at the Shrine of the Storm before it sailed. The Kul Tirans even drained a bay for more fields, holding the ocean back behind the wall at Fort Daelin. When the Alliance came looking for that navy in the Fourth War, they found the shrine's own priests had turned to the Queen of the Naga and the void beneath her, and the work stopped.

summary: Stormwind is the Alliance's working capital: a walled human city on the northwest coast of Elwynn Forest, its districts strung along canals beneath the Cathedral of Light, patrolled by the City Guard and quietly worked by SI:7. The throne is the Wrynn line's, though Anduin has spent years away from it and Turalyon has held the kingdom in his stead. Every Alliance race keeps a quarter, a shop or an embassy here, and the harbour and the Deeprun Tram make it the easiest place on Azeroth to leave from.
history: Arathi settlers under Faldir came south from Lordaeron roughly twelve centuries before the Dark Portal and founded a kingdom in a fertile valley on a continent they named Azeroth. The Wrynn line held it through a gnoll uprising and then a Gurubashi war that ended with the trolls at these walls, King Barathen dead in a counterattack and Medivh burning their army off the field. The orcs came next: a first siege broken when Lothar landed knights behind their lines, a second that got into the streets, and Garona's dagger in King Llane in front of his son. The survivors sailed for Lordaeron and burned the ships they could not take. Terenas paid for the rebuilding, the Stonemasons' Guild did the work and Turalyon brought the exiles home. The debt and the quarrel over that work were both being steered by Lady Katrana Prestor, a royal adviser who was the black dragon Onyxia; Varian unmasked her in the keep on his own return and hung her head from the gates. Deathwing tore the Park off the western flank in the Cataclysm and took the head away with him. Varian died on the Broken Shore a few years after that, and the ruined Park was rebuilt as Lion's Rest — his tomb, and the memorial for everyone else lost there — with Anduin crowned over it.

summary: Suramar is the centre of the Broken Isles and the last piece of the night elf empire still standing as a city rather than a ruin. Behind a shield that stayed up for ten thousand years its people became the nightborne, kept alive by the Nightwell, and Grand Magistrix Elisande has now handed both to the Legion. Outside the walls the rebels work out of Shal'Aran, the withered scavenge what the Nightwell would not give them, and the countryside is full of ley stations, collapsed Highborne towns, vrykul at Jandvik and naga in the eastern bay.
history: This was Illidan's home city, and Malfurion's, and Tyrande's. The Legion sacked it during the War of the Ancients, and the nathrezim used its dead for the experiments that would become the Scourge ten thousand years later. Its Highborne shut the second portal the demons opened, and when the Sundering came they raised a shield over the part of the city they could hold; the rest went to the sea floor. Under that shield they became the nightborne and grew wholly dependent on the Nightwell. When the demons returned and offered terms, Elisande took them; Thalyssra's attempt to stop her failed, and her rebels have been outside the walls, starving, ever since.

summary: The Swamp of Sorrows is the surviving northern half of the Black Morass: mud, standing water, crocolisks and spiders, east of Deadwind Pass and north of the Blasted Lands. The Temple of Atal'Hakkar lies drowned in the middle of it and is still watched by green dragons, and around it sit the Horde's rebuilt Stonard, the Alliance outpost at Marshtide Watch and Bogpaddle, a goblin resort happy to sell to both. The Broken at the Harborage and the feral Lost Ones at Fallow Sanctuary are the same refugees, divided only by who kept their mind.
history: The Atal'ai fled here when the Gurubashi Empire fell and raised a temple to Hakkar, meaning to pull the loa bodily into the world; their magic twisted everything around it, so Ysera sank the temple into the bog and left Eranikus to watch it. The orcs came through the Dark Portal into the same marshland and built three towns, of which only Stonard survived the First War. When the portal was destroyed the southern half of the Morass burned away into the Blasted Lands, and what was left took its name from the dead of the Second War. Kilrogg Deadeye's clan hid in these bogs for years and was still there when the Horde came back, and the Warsong fell back here once Draenor was destroyed. Draenei survivors, goblin developers and an Alliance garrison have settled in since.
factions: Kingdom of Stormwind and the Alliance
Murlocs and gilblins of the coast

summary: Talador is the middle of Draenor and the draenei's own country: rivers running down from the Sea of Zangar, olemba forests held in a permanent autumn, and the cathedral city of Shattrath at the crossroads. South of it lies Auchindoun, the vault where the draenei keep their dead. As things stand the Iron Horde has landed on the northern coast and taken Shattrath, the Legion's converts are working at Auchindoun, and the Alliance and Horde have each planted a fort in the north-east.
history: The Botani held Talador first, and it was here they grew a new sporemound to throw at the arakkoa of Arak, who burned the forest to ash to stop it. Ogres razed orc settlements across these woods centuries before the draenei landed. The draenei then made the region their heart: Shattrath at the river crossing, Auchindoun to the south to hold their souls, Tuurem on the road between the two and Telmor hidden in the trees. A Bladewind clan village near Shattrath was where Gul'dan first turned the orcs on the draenei, and the lie he told about the raid that destroyed it is what unified the clans. Warlord Blackhand has since taken the Orunai Coast and Shattrath itself for the Iron Horde, and the Sargerei have opened the way for Teron'gor to reach Auchindoun.
factions: Shadow Council and the Burning Legion

summary: Tanaan Jungle is the eastern peninsula of Draenor, the Bleeding Hollow clan's home ground and the place where the Iron Horde built its own Dark Portal. Cliffs and fortifications make the heart of it almost unreachable from the ground, which is exactly why the invasion was staged here and why Gul'dan kept it once the Legion had the Horde. Fel now runs down from Hellfire Citadel as the Felblight, and the Alliance at Lion's Watch and the Horde at Vol'mar hold beachheads against it.
history: The jungle grew out of a dead sporemound, and the Bleeding Hollow built a hard, superstitious culture around surviving flora that could kill them; the Bonechewers they cast out went cannibal in the same trees. In the timeline that produced Outland, this was where Blackhand's masons raised Hellfire Citadel as the first Horde's capital and where the original Dark Portal was cut into the eastern shore — after which fel magic dried the whole peninsula out and left it the Hellfire Peninsula. Here the Iron Horde built its own portal and poured through, and the counter-attack that shut it stranded its survivors on Draenor. Gul'dan then took the Horde off Grommash for the Legion, and the Felblight ran down from the citadel until it lay in a moat around it.

summary: Tanaris is the great desert of southeastern Kalimdor, rolling dunes under a cloudless sky with sandstorms crossing them and enormous cave systems running underneath. Gadgetzan is the Steamwheedle Cartel's capital and, since the Cataclysm put the sea at its doorstep, a port as well; the wreck of Steamwheedle Port down the coast belongs to the Southsea pirates now. The rest of the desert is other people's: Farraki sand trolls at Zul'Farrak, Dunemaul ogres and Wastewander bandits fighting over the only water, silithid in the Gaping Chasm, and the bronze dragonflight beneath it all at the Caverns of Time.
history: This was jungle once, tauren country and the edge of the Gurubashi Empire, until the Sundering broke the landmass and left sand — and left the Farraki stranded here to become sand trolls. The bronze dragons have always kept their home under it, and the titans left a way into Uldum in the southern mountains. When silithid hives out in the wastes struck at Anachronos, the bronze flight joined the War of the Shifting Sands in Silithus. Cho'gall's cult made a base in the caves and abandoned it once Garona started killing them one at a time. Later the Scourge came twice and C'Thun's armies once. The Cataclysm drowned Steamwheedle Port and made a beach town of Gadgetzan.

summary: Teldrassil is the World Tree the night elves grew in the Veiled Sea off northwestern Kalimdor, so vast that its crown carries a forested island with its own weather, rivers and wildlife — Darnassus in the west of it, Dolanaar on the road, Shadowglen in the northeast corner where night elf characters wake up, and the port of Rut'theran down among the roots. The Horde burned it during the War of the Thorns and the husk is still smouldering, so the green version anyone walks through now is the tree as it stood before the fire. Gnarlpine furbolgs and satyrs hold pockets of that forest, a corruption the night elves spent years trying to name.
history: Fandral Staghelm took over the Cenarion Circle while Malfurion was lost in the Emerald Dream, persuaded the Ancients of Darkshore, and grew the tree to win the kaldorei's immortality back. Nozdormu called the wish arrogant and withheld his blessing, so it never did. Worse, Fandral had grafted a branch of Xavius into it, which tied the tree to the Nightmare and is what drove the furbolgs mad. Malfurion cut the branch out on his return from the Dream; Alexstrasza blessed the tree belatedly, Ysera joined her at his wedding, and the last of the taint was forced out and destroyed. Then Sylvanas ordered it burned, in the largest fire Azeroth has seen, and the survivors scattered to Stormwind and Darkshore.

summary: Terokkar Forest fills the south of Outland with dusky green olemba pines, and it holds both the best and the worst of the continent: Shattrath City in the northwest, where the naaru and the draenei take in refugees of every race, and the Bone Wastes in the south, where the shattered mausoleum of Auchindoun sits in a crater of ash. Arakkoa hold the mountains at Skettis and the veils scattered through the trees, the Alliance and Horde keep towns at Allerian Stronghold and Stonebreaker Hold, and Kael'thas's blood elves, Shadow Council warlocks and fel orc remnants all have holdings in between.
history: This was Talador, red and orange olemba forest standing in perpetual autumn around Shattrath and around Auchindoun, the mausoleum raised to hold the remains of the naaru D'ore and the ancestral spirits it drew. Only the strip nearest the Spires of Arak was Terokkar then, and the arakkoa outcasts held it. Talador became the draenei's last stand; the orcs cut through to Shattrath once they had drunk Mannoroth's blood, and their fel magic bleached the trees to the dusky green they are now. Those who fled to Auchindoun held the crypts until Teron'gor's warlocks, losing, tore a hole in reality and pulled Murmur through it. The blast levelled the tomb city and the forest around it, and that is the Bone Wastes. The outcasts took the whole region afterwards and renamed it for Terokk, their lost king.

Bleeding Hollow and Bonechewer fel orcs

summary: Thaldraszus is the high country of the Dragon Isles and the dragons' seat of power — the one region where the architecture is still standing rather than sunk in moss. Valdrakken sits in its valley, Tyrhold's titan aqueducts run across it, the Algeth'ar Academy teaches again, and the bronze flight keeps the timeways from the Temporal Conflux. Beneath all of it is the Vault of the Incarnates, which is where the Primalists were headed the whole time.
history: When the Aspects settled the isles after the war with Galakrond, the keeper Tyr built them a waterworks in these mountains, and the dragons have revered him for it ever since he stopped being there to thank. From here the flights governed their kingdom and taught their young, until the Sundering drained the isles and everyone with wings left; the titan keepers stayed on and kept the machinery turning for ten thousand years without an audience. The flights came back to find it intact. They rebuilt their capital, reopened the academy, and then had to hold the vault under their own feet against the Primalists, who wanted the Incarnates sealed inside it out and elemental.

summary: The Azure Span is the cold half of the Dragon Isles: frozen lakes and stalled waterfalls, misty forest tundra, and ice cliffs climbing to the Vakthros range, all of it laid over old arcane ruins and leyline nexuses. The blue dragonflight's ground by right, but ten thousand years of absence left it to other people — the Iskaara tuskarr on the southwestern coast, gorlocs and furbolg in the woods, and the Brackenhide gnolls squatting on the ley crystals. The Kirin Tor came to study the leylines and stayed to fight over them.
history: Blue dragons held this country before the War of the Ancients. Their departure left the ley crystals unguarded, and the Brackenhide gnolls took the ground they sat in without ever grasping what they had. When the isles woke, the Kirin Tor arrived to read the arcane energies, the Dragonscale Expedition camped in the south, and the Primalists came for both — Camp Antonidas was attacked outright, and Zaqali djaradin planted a siege camp in the Upper Frostlands before the locals threw them out. Meanwhile the tuskarr were fighting gnolls whose magic had turned to rot, and their matriarch escaped the reckoning. Kalecgos came home to a flight in pieces, made common cause with the tuskarr, and used an echo of Sindragosa to wake the Azure Oathstone.

summary: The Cape of Stranglethorn is the southern tail of the vale, everything below the Gurubashi Arena, and Booty Bay is why anyone goes there. The goblin port built into the cliffs of the lagoon keeps a neutral auction house, a bank, trainers and a boat to Ratchet, and Baron Revilgaz runs it in permanent low-grade war with the Bloodsail Buccaneers offshore. Beyond the town the Horde has its resort at Hardwrench Hideaway, the Explorers' League digs near Mistvale Valley, and the arena still fills on schedule.
history: The arena on the cliffs above Booty Bay is Gurubashi work, left from an empire that once held the whole south of the continent, and so are the ruins strung along the coast below. Goblins took the lagoon afterwards and built a port in it, and the Steamwheedle Cartel has kept it profitably neutral since: anyone may trade there and nobody should be trusted. The cartel sold the Old Horde its charts, engineering and shipwrights for the invasion of Lordaeron, and was paid in Stormwind's plundered gold and treated as an equal for it. The Bloodsail Buccaneers wanted the harbour for themselves, were pushed out to a camp up the western shore, and have raided the lanes since. The Cataclysm cut the cape off from the jungle to the north, and Sassy Hardwrench landed her evacuated goblins not long after.

Naga and sea giants of the coast

summary: The Exodar is a wrecked starship the draenei live in: a piece of the naaru dimensional fortress Tempest Keep, stolen to escape Outland and brought down on the western shore of Azuremyst Isle, its halls still lit by arcane current and one whole district still too broken to enter. Velen guides its people and the Triumvirate of the Hand governs, with the vindicators of the Hand of Argus keeping order. It is the quietest capital in the Alliance and the furthest from anywhere.
history: The naaru built the ship, three of them shaping a district each, and it hung as part of Tempest Keep until Kael'thas seized the fortress and took M'uru for Silvermoon's magisters to drain. Velen led a raid to take one satellite back, and with the naaru O'ros aboard the draenei ran for Azeroth. Blood elf saboteurs got in first: the vessel lost control somewhere over northern Kalimdor, shedding crystal as it went, and came apart on the islands off Darkshore. The wreckage poisoned a whole neighbouring isle red. The survivors made the largest intact section their capital, and when it was finally repaired and the argument came to fly home to Outland, Velen said they would stay.

summary: The Forbidden Reach is the island off the Dragon Isles where Neltharion made the dracthyr and trained them, a place of storm-lashed coast, frozen spine and hollowed-out creches. It slept for an age after the battle that emptied it, and the dracthyr slept with it. It is awake now: the four weyrns are back on their old ground, morqut tuskarr have settled the western islet, and the Earth-Warder's workshops and the Zskera Vaults are being opened by people who did not build them.
history: Neltharion shaped the island as a proving ground for soldiers he designed himself, and the dracthyr were raised and drilled in creches sunk into it — one for war, one for siege, one to support and one to heal, each weyrn made for a purpose and told nothing else. A battle ended that, and the Earth-Warder sealed the island and everything in it. Nobody landed for ages; a flier who tried was struck out of the sky. The dracthyr woke when an old enemy stirred, and coming back they found their birthplace picked over — vaults broken open, tarasek in the tunnels, and a great deal of what Neltharion left behind still working.

summary: The Hinterlands are steep wooded mountains on the eastern edge of Lordaeron, and the ground is disputed between the Wildhammer dwarves at Aerie Peak, who breed and ride the gryphons the region is famous for, and the forest trolls whose empire began here. Vilebranch trolls hold Jintha'Alor and the Altar of Zul in the south, Witherbark the old temples in the middle, and the Revantusk, who took the Horde's offer, have a village on the coast. In the north stands Seradane, one of the four great trees, with a portal into the Emerald Dream and green dragons around it that the Nightmare has reached at least once.
history: The Amani Empire started in these hills and ruled most of eastern Lordaeron until the Troll Wars broke it: the high elves taught the Arathi arcane magic in exchange for their armies, and what survived was reduced to remnants here and in the north. The Wildhammers arrived after the War of the Three Hammers, giving up Grim Batol for life above ground at Aerie Peak, and the trolls have treated them as squatters ever since. They were isolated enough to learn of the Second War only when the Horde marched into it: Kurdran's gryphon riders bled the column from the clouds, Doomhammer threw half his army at Aerie Peak while the rest slipped north, and Lothar came to drive the orcs into the forest. Kurdran took the Alliance's oath afterwards. Only the landless Revantusk later took the New Horde's offer.

summary: The Jade Forest is the rainforest along Pandaria's eastern coast — bamboo, cloud-ringed spires and pandaren temples — and it is where both invading armies came ashore. Paw'don Village in the south has taken the Alliance's side and Honeydew Village in the northwest the Horde's, while Dawn's Blossom in the middle refuses to choose. Yu'lon's temple on the eastern shore, the first dungeon anyone new to the continent walks into, has been overrun by the Sha of Doubt.
history: The mogu ruled here first, and their work still stands: the Terrace of Ten Thunders in the north, with servants of the Thunder King waking inside it. Yu'lon's own story is local. Told she was teaching his pandaren slaves to think for themselves, Lei Shen pulled a bolt out of the sky and knocked her down into this forest, and the pandaren who found her dying have carved her a fresh jade body every hundred years since. The newest one was almost finished when the Alliance wrecked on the coast, the Horde followed to hunt Anduin Wrynn and Admiral Taylor, and the fighting at Serpent's Heart put it on the ground. Nobody outside Pandaria knew the statue was also the seal on the Sha of Doubt.
factions: Forest Hozen of the Grookin tribe
Mogu and the reawakened servants of the Thunder King

summary: The Lost Isles are a small tropical archipelago in the Great Sea between Kezan and the Maelstrom — jungle, raptors, a volcanic peak and a caldera full of pygmy villages. This is where the Bilgewater Cartel washed up after fleeing the eruption of Mount Kajaro, and where the goblins ended up joining the Horde before rebuilding in Azshara. The isles are reachable only during the goblin starting experience.
history: The islands' recorded history is mostly other people's shipwrecks. Fleeing Mount Kajaro aboard Trade Prince Gallywix's yacht — paying evacuees above deck, the ones he had put in chains below — the Bilgewater Cartel was attacked by an Alliance fleet and scattered across the beaches. The isles were already occupied: pygmy tribes at Oostan and Oomlot, Southsea Freebooters who rounded the castaways up again into slave pits, naga in the drowned ruins of Vashj'elan, and monkeys mining kaja'mite out of a cavern. The Horde's own ship, the Draka's Fury, went down offshore in the same waters, putting Thrall's orcs under Aggra on the same coast. The goblins fought their way clear, unpacked a town out of a crate, and left with the Horde when the peak erupted.

summary: The Maw is where the Shadowlands put the souls it had decided were beyond saving, and the Jailer is the only authority in it. There are no towns, no inns and nowhere to stop; the land itself belongs to Zovaal and rearranges to suit him, and his Eye finds anyone who stays too long. Torghast stands at the centre holding his most valuable prisoners, and since the machinery of death broke every soul that dies now arrives here regardless of what they did in life.
history: Zovaal was one of the Eternal Ones, given this realm and the keeping of the irredeemable. He decided the order the First Ones had laid down was worth overthrowing, and the others put him down, stripped him of his sigil and shut him inside the prison he had been running. It held for a very long time, and the Maw was a place nobody escaped and few would name. What broke it was the Arbiter being struck down: judgement stopped, every soul began falling here instead, and the realm swelled on them while the rest of the Shadowlands starved. Ve'nari's refuge was the first foothold anyone from outside managed to keep.

summary: The Ringing Deeps is the industrial layer of Khaz Algar, directly under the Isle of Dorn: forges, golem works, waterworks and mine after mine, all of it still running. The earthen Machine Speakers keep it going, and High Speaker Brinthe leads them and speaks for them on the Council of Dornogal. They share the caverns with kobold tribes, with Gallywix's goblins who arrived to sell them things, and with nerubians coming up from below.
history: The machinery here was sunk by the titan-forged, and the Speakers were made to tend it — a job description that means talking to machines rather than to people, carried out without interruption for thousands of years. Brinthe held a speakership for millennia and asked more questions than the office wanted; she was sent up to Dornogal to be out of the way. It turned out she was right to ask. In her absence the high speaker took his people into the Stonevault and the Void took him, and by the time anyone from the surface came down the works had kobolds in the tunnels, a goblin concern at the southern elevator, and nerubians using the river as a road.

summary: The Storm Peaks are the highest mountains in Northrend and some of the highest in the world, a country of blizzards, avalanches and winds that will take a climber off a ledge. Almost every summit carries titan work: the Terrace of the Makers, the Temple of Storms where Thorim sits, and the fortress-city of Ulduar. The living here are frost giants at Dun Niffelem, the hyldnir vrykul of Brunnhildar, frostborn dwarves at Frosthold, earthen driven out of Ulduar, iron dwarves, taunka on the high plateau at Camp Tunka'lo, and a goblin trading town called K3 at the bottom of it all.
history: Odyn had the Forge of Wills sunk into this range, and once the titans named him Prime Designate the keepers raised Ulduar above it — machine shops, libraries and Yogg-Saron's prison inside the same walls. Proximity told. The Old God worked on Loken until he killed Thorim's wife Sif and blamed the ice giants for it; the war that followed emptied the peaks of their makers. Loken had Helya tear Odyn's wing into the sky as the Halls of Valor and exiled the giants onto the mountainsides they still hold. He later lit the Forge again to turn out iron dwarves and vrykul for the thing beneath it, and Brann Bronzebeard went in after dwarven history and found that instead. Killing Loken tripped a titan failsafe: Algalon the Observer woke in Ulduar to weigh the planet and send Reply-Code Omega, the answer that has a world wiped and begun again. He was argued out of transmitting it, and the reply never left the peaks.

summary: The Waking Shores are where anyone sailing to the Dragon Isles lands first: a coast of geysers, hot springs and coloured rock that climbs west into volcanic mountains, and the old ground of the red and black dragonflights. The red flight keeps the Ruby Lifeshrine and its life pools in the southeast; the black flight's Obsidian Citadel sits in the heights, held for a long time by djaradin rather than dragons. The Dragonscale Expedition has its base camp here, and the Uktulut tuskarr the shoreline.
history: This was the Broodlands' seaward edge, and the black flight raised a fortress in the mountains above it so that the Earth-Warder could answer anything that came at the isles. Then the Sundering pulled the magic out of the land, the flights left, and their halls went to moss and rubble over ten thousand years. The djaradin who had hunted dragons here slept through most of it and woke when the isles did, taking the citadel and the northern coast, with the Qalashi the fiercest of them. So the expedition that made landfall found a place with two owners: Alexstrasza calling both mortal factions in to help her flight hold it, and Wrathion trying to take back a seat for a flight that hardly exists.

summary: The Wandering Isle is not an island. It is the shell of Shen-zin Su, a sea turtle grown big enough to carry villages, forest, farmland and small mountains, and it has been circling Azeroth since the pandaren who first rode it decided not to get off. This is where a pandaren character starts, at Master Shang Xi's training grounds, and since the Legion burned the Peak of Serenity it is also home to the monks who survived, gathered at the Temple of Five Dawns as the Order of the Broken Temple.
history: Liu Lang rode this turtle away from Pandaria to find out whether anything of the world had survived the Sundering, and his descendants never got off; over the centuries they stopped calling home at all. What ended that was a collision. The Skyseeker, an Alliance gunship carrying Horde prisoners, came out of the mist into Shen-zin Su's flank, and the prisoners walked free in the confusion — so both factions were ashore at once and the pandaren took sides around them. Ji Firepaw blew the wreck clear rather than pick it out, which opened the wound instead of closing it and left the turtle dying and drifting towards the Maelstrom. Horde druids and Alliance priests had to heal him together.

summary: Thousand Needles is a canyon of towering rock spires in southern Kalimdor with the sea in it. The Shattering let the water in and turned the floor of the canyon into the Shimmering Deep, so the mesa-top camps and towns that used to look down on centaur warbands now look down on a lake, and Fizzle & Pozzik's Speedbarge floats where the Mirage Raceway used to run. The Great Lift is broken, entire centaur clans drowned, and what moved in afterwards is worse: Southsea pirates at their holdfast, the Twilight's Hammer on the heights, and the Grimtotem still at Darkcloud Pinnacle.
history: Water cut these needles out of the rock over centuries, and the tauren built on top of them to stay above the centaur who ranged the canyon floor — Freewind Post fought the Galak and the Grimtotem from up there with Horde help for years. Out east, on the salt flats, goblins and gnomes raced rocket cars at the Mirage Racetrack to settle which of them built better engines. C'Thun's armies came through during the war in Silithus. Then Deathwing returned and the sea poured in, drowning the flats, the lift and most of the Galak, and the two rival engineers moored a barge over the wreck of their own speedway. The Legion later hit the Grimtotem hard enough that Magatha asked the Earthen Ring for help.

summary: Thunder Bluff is the tauren capital: four mesas standing several hundred feet over the grass of northern Mulgore, roped together by bridges and reachable only by wooden lift, wyvern or zeppelin. Baine Bloodhoof rules the united tribes from the chieftain's tent, with the Cenarion Circle on Elder Rise and the shaman keeping the Pools of Vision on Spirit Rise. It is a trade city and a hunters' refuge, and the least fortified capital either faction has.
history: The tauren spent centuries moving, harried by centaur, until the Third War brought Thrall's orcs into Mulgore and the two together drove the raiders off. Cairne Bloodhoof settled his people on the mesas and the scattered tribes came in under his banner, and the city was raised as a place any tribe could come to. It held until Garrosh Hellscream killed Cairne in a rigged duel and Magatha Grimtotem used the moment to seize the bluffs, murdering druids, shaman and the whole Skychaser tribe as she went. Baine bought weapons, came back by zeppelin, split her forces and took the city; Magatha went into exile and he has been high chieftain since.

summary: The Timeless Isle sits east of the Jade Forest and is, for the moment, findable at all — it drifts in and out of Pandaria's mists, and while it is here the sun never moves off sunset. The Celestial Court in the middle is where the August Celestials test whoever turns up; the Ordon yaungol hold the heights around their fire god, and the shoreline below is a scramble of chests, rare beasts and timeless coins. Two small pandaren beachheads sit on the western shore and have been asked politely not to go further in.
history: The island was a proving ground. Pandaren came to be judged in front of the Celestials on wisdom, hope, strength and fortitude, following the example Emperor Shaohao set, and they lived alongside a yaungol tribe who built their entire culture on fire — the Ordon, whose shaman burned himself into a demigod. Then the place vanished. What the scrolls record since is glimpses at a distance, in a different position each time, and adventurers who went ashore during those glimpses were lost to the Timeways and never came home. It has surfaced again, which is what drew the bronze dragonflight, pandaren scholars and the black dragon Wrathion. Even lately, visitors have found it unreachable as often as not.

summary: Tiragarde Sound is the middle and largest of Kul Tiras' three regions, a rugged stretch of hills and forest split nearly in two by a bay that runs from one side of the island to the other. Boralus sits on that strait, seat of House Proudmoore and of the kingdom itself, so every road and shipping lane in Kul Tiras passes through here. The people of the Sound are sailors, monster hunters and nobles in roughly equal measure, and they share the coast with the pirate fleets of Freehold.
history: The Sound is where the Proudmoores come from, and their rise made Boralus the capital of a kingdom built on the sea. Its people learned to hunt the things the ocean threw at them and to fight the raiders who worked the same water, tolerating the free port at Freehold so long as it stayed offshore. By the Fourth War that arrangement had broken down: the Irontide were striking the mainland, House Ashvane's money was quietly backing them from Bridgeport, and the nobles were too busy with each other to notice. The Alliance arrived to court Kul Tiras, made Boralus its base for the war against the Horde, and left with a navy.

summary: Tirisfal Glades is the Forsaken's home ground on the northern coast of Lordaeron, wooded hills under a permanently green-tinted sky where the plague never really left the soil. Brill is the town, Deathknell the village the newly risen wake up in, and the Ruins of Lordaeron stand over the Undercity, which has been uninhabitable since the Battle for Lordaeron. The Scarlet Crusade keeps its monastery and outposts here, Scourge remnants hold Agamand Mills and the abandoned farms, and the whole glade is named for a titan keeper who died in it.
history: The name is vrykul for Tyr's Fall. The keeper died here fighting the C'Thrax Zakajz, and both were buried where they fell beneath his silver hand; vrykul settled to guard the tomb, their cursed children grew into something else, and humanity began in this glade. Dath'Remar's exiled Highborne landed here next, but whatever lies under the ground began driving them mad and they moved north to found Quel'Thalas instead. Thoradin won the Tirisfal tribe by pilgrimage rather than force, and the country they held was later named Lordaeron for their general. The Second War arrived without warning: Doomhammer came out of Alterac's passes into these glades and had the capital under bombardment before the Alliance knew he had crossed. The plague took all of it during the Third War, and Sylvanas's free-willed dead took what the Scourge left behind. The Alliance came for the capital at the opening of the Fourth War, put Brill down to its foundations and drove Sylvanas out of the throne room; she answered by venting blight over the ground between the town and the ruins, which is why nothing grows on it and why the Undercity is shut. The Forsaken hold the glades again, without their city.

summary: Tol Barad is a fortified island west of Gilneas that has been a battlefield, a ruin and a magical prison in turn. Baradin Hold sits at its centre holding things nobody could safely destroy — demons among them — and the Baradin's Wardens who guard it are no longer entirely reliable. The island is fought over as an outdoor PvP objective: the Wardens for the Alliance, Hellscream's Reach for the Horde, and whoever holds the three fortifications holds the Hold.
history: Arathor raised the citadel more than twelve centuries ago and Stromgarde held the island after the empire came apart. In the Second War the Alliance staged from it to retake Dun Modr, and the orcs answered by storming the place, razing the fortress and killing most of the people on it. Kul Tiran arcanists claimed the ruin afterwards, rebuilt the walls and turned the defences inward: a prison for what could not safely be killed, kept by a Stromic and Tirasian garrison who became the Baradin's Wardens. The Cataclysm made it a front again when Garrosh sent Hellscream's Reach to take it, and while the two armies traded the island back and forth something inside Baradin Hold began driving the wardens mad — guards opening cells, the long-dead getting up to fight their last battle again.

summary: Townlong Steppes is the northern half of the land on the wrong side of the Serpent's Spine: red-leafed hills, bare crags in the northeast, and a scatter of islands off the western coast. Niuzao's temple stands on one of those islands and has been besieged twice, first by mantid out of the Dread Wastes and then by mogu. The Shado-Pan hold the rest from a garrison and a handful of outposts, hunting the Sha of Hatred while Osul yaungol raid out of their fire camp below the Ox Gate.
history: The mantid have thrown themselves at the wall on a hundred-year rhythm for as long as anyone has kept records, and these hills are where they land. This time they came a decade early and got through, which told the pandaren the fault lay with the mantid rather than with the wall. The Sha of Hatred, loose from the Kun-Lai monastery, came west and set the yaungol killing each other along the border; Taran Zhu followed it, held the Gao-Ran line while the swarm threw everything it had at the blockade, and finally cornered it in the kypari Kri'vess. Then the mantid massed again on Niuzao's island temple under an empress the Sha of Fear had taken, and after that came Shan Bu's mogu.
