summary: The Twilight Highlands are the northeastern corner of Khaz Modan, a coastal highland that used to be pleasant and is now half-swallowed by Void corruption bleeding out of the Twilight's Hammer's citadel. Wildhammer dwarves hold the north and west, Dragonmaw orcs the south and the port, and the red dragonflight keeps a watch from the Vermillion Redoubt over the cursed fortress of Grim Batol. Ogres, naga and twilight dragonkin fill in the gaps.
history: The Wildhammers returned to Grim Batol after the War of the Three Hammers and found Modgud's curse still in the stone; most left for the Hinterlands and the rest settled the highlands nearby. The Dragonmaw orcs who survived Grim Batol built a fortress on the coast, and the two have fought over the ground ever since. Then Cho'gall brought the Twilight's Hammer here, carved the Bastion of Twilight out of a spire, and the Void seeping from it warped the land and gave the region its present name. Both factions came for it during the war on Deathwing — Kurdran Wildhammer uniting the dwarf clans, Garrosh buying the Dragonmaw with promises of blood. Deathwing fought Alexstrasza above Grim Batol and left wounded; Cho'gall died in his own citadel. The corruption has not receded.

summary: Uldum is a titan facility with a desert on top of it, filling the southern end of Kalimdor: dunes, half-buried pyramids and one green river running through the middle of them. It belongs to the tol'vir, split between the Ramkahen who kept faith with the titans and the Neferset who sold themselves to Deathwing for their stone bodies back. Everyone else here — Al'Akir's air elementals, Commander Schnottz's diggers, the Explorers' League and the Reliquary — came for the machinery underneath.
history: Highkeeper Ra brought the tol'vir, anubisaths and mogu south and set the Forge of Origination here, machinery that steadies the deep earth and, at full power, would strip the planet of life to start it over. Ra vanished into the catacombs, and the soldiers Loken sent after him carried the Curse of Flesh — which is why tol'vir are flesh at all and why Deathwing had something to offer them. Thousands of years on the mogu emperor Lei Shen marched on the Forge for the eternal life in it; the tol'vir fired it at its lowest setting, killing him, his army and the country — sand ever since. They hid the passes behind magic. The Cataclysm tore that ward off and Al'Akir came through a rift for the Forge; both factions reached the machine first, then went into Skywall after him. Sargeras's sword unsealed further tombs a generation later and the Amathet came out of one — tol'vir who hold every other tol'vir a traitor to the titans' work and mean to keep the Halls of Origination to themselves. The Ramkahen made common cause with the Explorers' League and the Wastewander bandits to stop them, and that alliance, the Uldum Accord, held the Halls against the Amathet and against N'Zoth's forces at the same time.

summary: Undercity was the Forsaken capital, a ring of quarters dug into Lordaeron's old crypts and sewers beneath the ruined palace in Tirisfal Glades — and Sylvanas blighted it herself rather than hand it to the Alliance. The catacombs below are still poison. What is walkable now is the surface: the courtyard, the bell, the throne room where Arthas killed his father and King Terenas' memorial, retaken and cleaned by the Desolate Council, who govern the Forsaken in Sylvanas' place.
history: The name is older than the undead who took it — beneath Lordaeron's palace lay the royal crypts, the dungeons and the sewers, and the city's poorest lived there among the prisoners. Orgrim Doomhammer was locked in these cells after the Second War and got out of them again, and nobody has explained how. After the Scourge razed the capital, Arthas set a work crew to hollow out something bigger and was recalled to Northrend before it was done. Sylvanas' breakaway undead won the war for the ruins that followed, named themselves the Forsaken and completed the maze. It survived a coup by Varimathras and Putress, and a joint Horde and Alliance assault that Jaina had to freeze before the two sides destroyed each other. At the opening of the Fourth War Sylvanas abandoned it and drowned it in blight.

summary: Undermine is the goblin capital, a city of tunnels, vaults and lava tubes wound through Mount Kajaro under the Isle of Kezan, with air like a hot workshop. The part anyone walks is downtown: the Gallagio casino on its hill, the tenements of Hovel Hill, Blackwater Marina, the Vatworks and the Heaps, with rockets at Slam Central Station running out to the districts nobody shows visitors. Gallywix ran it as Overboss until the city pulled him down, and Gazlowe and the cartel heads have been putting it back together since.
history: The Zandalari worked goblin slaves in these shafts for kaja'mite, and the ore made the miners clever enough to throw them off; the camps they revolted from became the city. Genius did not last — the kaja'mite ran out, the goblins got ordinary again and turned to selling things instead, after a stretch of gang wars nobody misses. Deathwing set Kajaro erupting during the Cataclysm and for a while everyone assumed Kezan was slag. Then Gallywix came home with a promise to Xal'atath to keep, took the cartels one hostage at a time, called himself Overboss and put Darkfuse enforcers in the streets. When his gunman killed Renzik in front of a crowd, the city marched on his casino.

summary: Un'Goro Crater is a bowl of steaming jungle dropped into the middle of southern Kalimdor's deserts, walled off from Tanaris, Silithus and Uldum by its own rim. Devilsaurs and other dinosaurs range it freely, a volcano called Fire Plume Ridge burns at the centre, and strange crystals and titan machinery are scattered through the undergrowth for anyone willing to survive long enough to study them. The people here are a handful of explorers and profiteers — Marshal's Stand, Mossy Pile — and everything else is either very large or watching from the Shaper's Terrace.
history: Freya built this crater as a place to experiment, one of three sites where the Well of Eternity's power had pooled, and Wild Gods came out of cradles like it. She worked from the Shaper's Terrace, and when she left, the watcher Nablya took over the observing; in Un'Goro the titan watchers are permitted to interfere directly, which they are not elsewhere. During the War of the Shifting Sands the qiraji drove the night elf army back through the crater and then could not take it — nobody has satisfactorily explained why. Much later the Marshal expedition arrived to catalogue it, was overrun twice, and rebuilt higher up each time. The Cult of the Damned briefly held the Terrace during the Northrend war.

summary: Valdrakken is the dragons' own capital, set in a bowl of Thaldraszus below the waterfalls and the aqueduct that runs down from Tyrhold, with the Seat of the Aspects at its centre and an enclave for each flight around it. The Valdrakken Accord governs from here — Alexstrasza, Nozdormu, Kalecgos, Merithra, Ebyssian and the Incarnate Vyranoth sharing a table — and the Scalesworn keep order in the streets. Mortals are welcome: the Dragonscale Expedition, the Artisan's Consortium and a black market all trade in it.
history: The dragons built it in the ancient era of the Dragon Isles and ruled Azeroth from it, each flight taking a quarter of the city and the Aspects meeting at the top. The Sundering drained the isles of the magic that made all of it possible, and the flights left — the city was handed to the titanic watchers, drakonid and dragonspawn who stayed behind, and it waited about ten thousand years. When the isles woke, the flights came back to it with mortal allies in tow and founded the Accord in its halls. It has been quietly contested since: Primalist agitators working the crowds, and a rebellion of drakonid and dragonspawn who had spent an age being talked past, who came within a detonator of collapsing the aqueduct.

summary: The Vale of Eternal Blossoms is the golden bowl at the centre of Pandaria, sealed off for thousands of years and reopened when the war arrived on the continent. Its eastern half is wrecked: Garrosh Hellscream's diggers tore the Heart of Y'Shaarj out of the ground, the sacred pools went with it, and a tree planted by Shaohao's spirit is what stands in the crater. The Shrine of Seven Stars and the Shrine of Two Moons are the two war capitals here, and Mogu'shan Palace on the eastern edge was the mogu empire's seat.
history: Freya made this a cradle of life, the same work as Un'Goro and Sholazar, and the Wild Gods who became the August Celestials came out of it. The jinyu rose from the vale's pools and governed Pandaria until Lei Shen took it from them by slaughter. After he died the mogu moved their imperial seat here, ruled the continent from Mogu'shan Palace, and turned the waters to the work of holding the pandaren down; when the pandaren threw them out, the Celestials sealed the basin and left it to the Golden Lotus. Xuen reopened it for outsiders who passed his trials, over the Shado-Pan's objection, and the mogu came straight back for it. A warlord massing at Mogu'shan pushed hundreds of warriors up the hidden path above Guo-Lai and reached the palace steps before the Golden Lotus and the champions they had recruited put him down; Xin the Weaponmaster then gathered the surviving clans under his own banner while the Shao-Tien came at the basin from the west, and that push got inside Mogu'shan itself. Both attempts were groundwork for the Thunder King's return.

summary: The Valley of the Four Winds is Pandaria's farmland, a wide plain of rolling fields and pools fed by water running down out of the Vale, which is why the vegetables grown here come up the size of a person. Halfhill's market sits dead centre and is the Tillers' home ground; the Stormstout Brewery stands at the western end. That end is closed by the Serpent's Spine, and the mantid behind it are pushing hard enough that the wall has started to crack.
history: Farmers have worked this plain for as long as anyone has bothered counting, watered by streams off the Vale, and the corn and lotus they grew fed an empire. They also built its wall: Lei Shen set the valley's pandaren to raising the Serpent's Spine along their western edge, a job that took generations and ended up running the length of the continent. Behind it the mantid hatch a killing generation every century, and the valley sits on their road. The Stormstouts brewed at the western end until the family scattered, and Chen came back generations later to a brewhall full of things that should not have been in it — in time to drill the farmers into a militia when the swarm arrived ten years early.

summary: Val'sharah is the forested north-west of the Broken Isles and the place druidism was invented: Cenarius taught it here, Malfurion learned it here, and the woods were shaped deliberately to sit as close to the Emerald Dream as waking ground can. The World Tree Shaladrassil stands over the north of it, and the Nightmare has taken the tree. Xavius' satyrs are pushing that corruption outward, the Dreamweavers hold the Dreamgrove against it, and the Gilneans of Bradensbrook are simply trying to live on the coast.
history: Cenarius kept this forest when Kalimdor was still whole, and taught the first night elf druid in it; his students then shaped the woods into an echo of the Emerald Dream, and Shaladrassil was planted to watch over them. The Ravencrests cut Black Rook Hold out of the rock and rose on the strength of it. The War of the Ancients cost the forest dearly: the Wild God Ashamane died killing a pit lord here, buying Suramar the hours it needed to raise its shield, and Illidan drained the Moon Guard to hold Black Rook. Afterwards the defeated satyrs were put to sleep under Shaladrassil's roots, which is where the Nightmare found them.

summary: Vashj'ir is a drowned night elf city and the sea floor around it, off the western coast of the Eastern Kingdoms, and the only zone in Azeroth played entirely underwater. The naga of the Nazjatar Empire hold it, contested by kvaldir raiders, gilblins, faceless ones and whatever the Earthen Ring and the two factions have managed to land there. It has no night: the kelp forests and the ruins glow from something nobody has explained.
history: Vashj'ir was one of the royal seats of Azshara's empire, ruled by Matron Lestharia Vashj. The Sundering dropped the whole of it beneath the Great Sea, and Azshara and the Highborne who went down with her were not killed but dragged into the Maelstrom and remade as naga — Lestharia's daughter Vashj, the queen's handmaiden and later Illidan's lieutenant, among the first — and raised Nazjatar on the sea floor. Ten thousand years on she sent Lady Naz'jar back, not for the ruins but for the rift under them: Vashj'ir opens onto the Abyssal Maw, and N'Zoth wanted Neptulon's command of the oceans rather than his death, which would have cut every sea route between continents. The Earthen Ring raised the alarm, both factions sailed, Ozumat sank their fleets, and the shipwrecked survivors broke the naga from the seabed up.

summary: The Voidstorm is a world remade by the Void, sitting at the nexus where Void energies across the cosmos converge, and it is the staging ground from which Xal'atath launched her assault on the Sunwell. Everything alive here survives by devouring something weaker, presided over by the domanaar and by Xal'atath's Devouring Host. It is not the Void's homeworld — it is a planet that was taken.
history: Long before the Void claimed it, this was a world called Predacea, rich in scholarship and crowned with cities that hung in its sky. A war between its empires grew ruinous enough that one side commissioned the weaponsmith Akintunde to end it outright; the weapon he built did exactly that, razing the civilisation it was meant to save, and his employers imprisoned him in the last days before the end. Only the smallest life came through, and over aeons it evolved into something relentlessly predatory. Void creatures settled the ruins afterwards. With Dimensius sealed inside the Dark Heart, Xal'atath siphoned that power to birth the Voidstorm here, then loosed it against Quel'Danas — where the Vanguard of the Light held it at the Sunwell until Magister Umbric found a way to cross over and strike back.

summary: Vol'dun is the desert filling the northwest of Zandalar — dunes, salt flats and broken rock from one coast to the other, littered with the bleached bones of enormous animals. Until recently the Zandalari used it as a death sentence, exiling criminals into it with no way back. The sethrak consider it holy ground and are split between Vorrik's Devoted and Korthek's Faithless, and the vulpera caravans survive in the gaps between them.
history: This was jungle once, and the Zandalari shared it with the sethrak, both peoples worshipping the serpent loa Sethraliss together. Around sixteen thousand years ago the C'Thraxxi warbringer Mythrax came through in the war against the aqir and killed trolls and sethrak alike, destroying the disc at the heart of the titan pyramid Atul'Aman. Sethraliss spent her own life to stop him. Between her death and the upheavals that followed the jungle dried to sand and the trolls left. Three sethrak sealed Mythrax inside the pyramid; one of them, Korthek, later decided he wanted the C'Thrax loose and an empire of his own, and split his people in two over it.

summary: The Western Plaguelands are where the plague was first let into Lordaeron, and they are also the half that has largely been taken back: the Cenarion Circle lifted most of the blight during the Cataclysm, and crops grow again on farms that used to be cauldron sites. The Argent Crusade runs its Lordaeron operation out of Hearthglen and trains recruits there, while Andorhal, fought over by Alliance and Forsaken death knights, ended up in Forsaken hands. Caer Darrow out in Darrowmere Lake is the largest thing the Scourge still holds, with Scholomance beneath it.
history: This was forest and farmland, Hearthglen the seat of the local administration and Andorhal the point every sack of northern Lordaeron's grain passed through — which is exactly why it was chosen. Kel'Thuzad's cultists infected the grain and hid plague cauldrons on four of the largest farms, and the countryside died and stood back up. The Scarlet Crusade held Mardenholde Keep at Hearthglen for years afterwards. Agents of the Argent Dawn eventually turned the cauldrons' contents against the Scourge, Tirion Fordring reclaimed his own town for the Argent Crusade, and the Cenarion Circle undid most of the corruption. The Battle for Andorhal between Thassarian and Sylvanas's forces settled who keeps the ruins.

summary: Westfall is Stormwind's ruined breadbasket, a coast of yellowed pasture and empty farmhouses where rogue harvest golems still clank through the fields and carrion birds work the rest. Sentinel Hill is the seat of the Westfall Brigade, who broke the Defias Brotherhood twice; Moonbrook and the mine beneath it were the Brotherhood's own ground, and the mine is the Deadmines. Since the surviving stonemasons were pardoned the farmers have begun again as the Breadbasket Guild, though drifters and the homeless still fill the sheds.
history: Westfall fed the kingdom for centuries and was burned three times for it: by gnolls whose assaults on the capital were a feint that left the farms uncovered; by a Gurubashi raiding party that slipped the patrols and put three towns to the torch, which is what sent Stormwind to war in the jungle; and by orc raiders in the First War. What finished it was not war but debt. The Stonemasons Guild went unpaid for rebuilding Stormwind, Onyxia worked both sides of the quarrel, and when Edwin VanCleef pressed for the money the guild was dissolved; the riots killed Queen Tiffin, and the masons fled here as the Defias Brotherhood. A decade of banditry drove off farmers and garrison alike, and the harvests stopped. Vanessa VanCleef raised the Brotherhood again after the Cataclysm and burned Sentinel Hill.

summary: The Wetlands are a cold grey marsh below the broken Stonewrought Dam, mist on the ground and mountains on three sides with the open sea on the fourth. Menethil Harbor is the Alliance port here and the sailing point for Kalimdor and Northrend, though the Cataclysm put a good deal of it under water. Dragonmaw orcs hold the Angerfang camp, gnolls the fen and Bluegill murlocs the shallows, night elves keep a grove around the plant-man of local legend, and Grim Batol sits shut at the eastern end.
history: The Wildhammers built their capital at Grim Batol after Ironforge fell out with itself, and left it when the Dark Iron invasion had fouled the mountain past living in; Ironforge later threw the Thandol Span across the canyon to keep the two dwarven countries joined. Doomhammer refused that crossing in the Second War and had his invasion fleet built instead in a hidden anchorage on this coast, goblin shipwrights and troll boatbuilders working under guard, while the Dragonmaw held Grim Batol; the marsh was stripped near bare feeding orcs and dragons. The Alliance took the coast back and rebuilt the yard as Menethil Harbor, named for Lordaeron's king — which is why Ner'zhul's death knights came back to it to steal ships. Freed red dragons broke the Dragonmaw, and the Cataclysm drowned the western marsh.

summary: Winterspring is a snowbound valley in the far northeast of Kalimdor, deep pine forest and frozen lakes with mountain giants, wildkin and wintersabers moving through it. Everlook sits at the crossroads of its trade routes, a Steamwheedle post that will sell to anyone; Starfall Village is the night elves' end of the valley, and Mazthoril, the great ice cavern near Lake Kel'Theril, is the blue dragonflight's home on this continent. The Ruins of Kel'Theril on the lakeshore are haunted by everyone who has ever come here after the same cursed crystal.
history: Blue dragons have lived in this valley since long before anyone counted, Haleh among them. Ten thousand years ago the Highborne city of Kel'Theril stood by the lake; its people stole the Crystal of Zin-Malor out of the temple at Eldarath, and playing with it broke both the crystal and them. The Sundering finished the city and its dead have not left. High elves under Archmage Maenius came for the shards a century before the Dark Portal and joined the ghosts; blood elves tried the same thing before the Cataclysm and were turned into wretched for it. In the Third War Tyrande and Malfurion cleared the valley and woke the Druids of the Talon in its barrow dens.

summary: Zangarmarsh is a luminous swamp west of Hellfire Peninsula, roofed by mushrooms the size of trees and lit from below by its own phosphorescent flora. It belongs to the sporeling colony of Sporeggar, three tribes of Lost Ones, and the ogres and naga taking pieces of it — Lady Vashj's followers drained lake after lake into the Coilfang Reservoir and still hold ground here. The Cenarion Expedition set up at the Cenarion Refuge to work out what was killing the marsh, and the Alliance and Horde each keep a foothold at Telredor and Zabra'jin.
history: The marsh is what is left of the Zangar Sea, grown from the rotting sporemound Zang; the fungal bloom that made it spread inland from Zangarra. When Shattrath was given up as lost, Velen brought the civilians here to Telredor, a shrine on an island the artificers hid behind a lattice of arcanite crystals. Survivors kept arriving, and those the orcs' red pox had deformed into Broken were driven back out by their own people; the Lost One tribes descend from them. Fel magic dried the sea into swamp. Lady Vashj settled it much later, enslaved the Wastewalker Broken and built pumping machines on every major lake to drain the water into Coilfang Reservoir, meaning to hold Outland by holding its water. The Alliance went in after her, struck the chains off the Broken and killed her there.

summary: Zaralek Cavern is the enormous cave system under the Dragon Isles, reached through a mouth in the hills between the Ohn'ahran Plains and Valdrakken. Two peoples live down here and neither had much interest in surface politics until the surface arrived: the molelike niffen of Loamm and the drogbar of Glimmerogg, who race snails and lift heavy things. Above them in the rock sit the Zaqali djaradin's caldera and Aberrus, Neltharion's hidden laboratory, directly beneath the citadel he defended the isles from.
history: The Earth-Warder wanted somewhere the other Aspects could not look, and he dug it here. Aberrus is where his worst work was done, and the shadow chamber inside it is where he first answered the Old Gods — every later thing Deathwing did began in this cave. Long after he was gone, the niffen and the drogbar made their own lives underground while the Zaqali held the volcanic south, and a titan facility sat quietly in the southeast. Then Raszageth died on the surface and the Primalists came looking for older allies. Iridikron went down into the deep, everyone chasing him followed, and the crucible was opened by people who did not know what was still in it.

summary: Zereth Mortis is the First Ones' workshop, folded into the fabric of the Shadowlands and closed to everybody until the Jailer forced it open. Afterlives are manufactured here, at an enormous Forge floating over the middle of the realm, and the mechanical automa left behind to run the process have kept working at it without supervision for longer than anyone can count. The Sepulcher of the First Ones sits at the far end of it, holding knowledge that would let whoever reached it rewrite what is real.
history: Nothing about this realm was meant to be found. The First Ones built it, staffed it with automa, and left; the brokers who venerate them could argue about what its name even translates to. Zovaal spent his imprisonment working out how to get in, and once he held all five sigils of the Eternal Ones he tore his way through — he had already ripped a piece of the place loose and chained it inside Torghast, and the wound that left is still visible. The Primus forged a key out of the four replacement sigils the covenants made and followed him. The Enlightened taught the mortals who came after how to read the automa's language, which is what made the realm navigable at all.

summary: Zul'Aman is the Amani homeland in the southeast of Quel'Thalas: forest, bog and coast around a walled temple city, with shrines to the beast loa Nalorakk, Akil'zon, Jan'alai and Halazzi at its heart. What is left of a forest troll empire lives here, along with the Revantusk, Witherbark, Shadowpine, Vilebranch and Spiritpaw who share the province, under Zul'jan and his sister Zul'jarra. The Twilight's Blade has come into the country with Void magic, took the temple city outright, and has only lately been pushed back off it.
history: The Zandalari and their allies killed the C'Thrax Kith'ix on this ground sixteen thousand years ago and built on the spot; it grew into a temple city and then into the strongest empire in the Eastern Kingdoms. Elves and the humans of Arathor ended that at the Troll Wars, and the Amani never held anything beyond this province again — though they never stopped hating the people who built Silvermoon over their burial ground. Zul'jin took them into the Old Horde, was captured and tortured by Farstriders, and died in his own halls when the Horde sent champions to kill him. Daakara reunited them with Zandalari backing and went the same way. Then the Void cult arrived.

summary: Zuldazar is the southern third of Zandalar and the seat of the Zandalari Empire, a golden temple city of stepped pyramids built along the highest peaks with jungle running down to the sea below it. Dazar'alor stands at its centre, the oldest continuously inhabited city on Azeroth and the harbour of the Golden Fleet. Blood trolls press the Blood Gate from Nazmir, and since the empire opened its doors the Horde keeps an embassy inside the palace itself.
history: Trolls settled these peaks because the loa lived on them, and the shrines the Zandalar tribe raised on the highest of them grew into the temple city that every other troll nation traces itself back to. Kings were entombed at Atal'Dazar for thousands of years and envoys from every tribe came here every sixth year to talk. The Cataclysm cracked the city open, flooded its forum and left the palace leaning, and it was rebuilt. Then the blood trolls came up out of the swamp, Princess Talanji went looking for allies and found the Horde, and the prophet Zul turned on his own king. The Alliance answered by sailing into the harbour, killing Rastakhan and burning much of the fleet.

summary: Zul'Drak is eastern Northrend's ice troll country, and it is less a region with a city in it than a city the size of a region: terraced plazas, aqueducts and ziggurats running to the horizon, with the capital of Gundrak at the top. The Drakkari who built it are losing it — pressed by the Scourge, they began killing and consuming their own loa for power, and much of what remains of them is deranged or already undead. The Argent Crusade holds the Argent Stand, the Knights of the Ebon Blade keep the Ebon Watch, and a Zandalari expedition has come north to save what it can of the loa and to write down the rest.
history: The Drakkari came north as an army. Hunting the aqir to extinction after the insects nearly finished the trolls, the Zandalari sent their fiercest tribes out with the promise of keeping whatever ground they cleared; the Drakkari drew the frozen end of it, fought an aqir colony and the titan-forged the insects had turned against them, and stayed. What they raised here became one of the largest troll nations that ever stood, and it outlasted Azjol-Nerub and every winter since. It did not outlast the Scourge. When Drakuru turned traitor and began raising blighted chieftains, the Drakkari butchered their own loa for the strength to hold, which did not save them and left the land stained with the gods' suffering rather than the Scourge's work. The Zandalari came to intervene and stayed to chronicle the end.
